title: The image of the USSR and its athletes at the 1952 Summer Olympic Games in the Soviet periodical press
title_original: The image of the USSR and its athletes at the 1952 Summer Olympic Games in the Soviet periodical press
summary: The purpose of the study is to identify the components and characteristics of the image of the Soviet Union and its athletes based on publications in domestic periodicals. Research methods: the content analysis method was used to systematize publications of periodical print media dedicated to the 1952 Olympic Games. For a more accurate interpretation of the use of specific statements in different texts, the discourse analysis method was employed. Research results and conclusions. Key points contained in the publications of the Soviet central and local periodicals regarding the 1952 Olympic Games have been identified. The main characteristics of the image of the Soviet state and its athletes have been revealed, related not only to achieving high sports results but also to addressing foreign policy objectives in the context of the Cold War. It has been established that the Soviet periodical press, being one of the main sources of information in the early 1950s, was used as an important tool for shaping the image of the USSR as a global sports power in the mass consciousness of citizens.

title: СПОРТСМЕНЫ КИТАЙСКОЙ НАРОДНОЙ РЕСПУБЛИКИ НА ИГРАХ ОЛИМПИАДЫ (ЛЕТНИХ ОЛИМПИЙСКИХ ИГРАХ)
title_original: СПОРТСМЕНЫ КИТАЙСКОЙ НАРОДНОЙ РЕСПУБЛИКИ НА ИГРАХ ОЛИМПИАДЫ (ЛЕТНИХ ОЛИМПИЙСКИХ ИГРАХ)
summary: В статье обобщены результаты выступления сборной команды КНР на летних Олимпийских играх в период с 1952 по 2024 годы. Полученные данные позволили установить, какие олимпийские виды спорта наиболее развиты в Китае, и увидеть те, которые только начинают обретать популярность. В статье также упомянуты выступления сборных Тайваня (Китайский Тайбэй) и Гонконга, самостоятельно выставляющих свои сборные для участия в Играх Олимпиад независимо от КНР

title: Event-driven changes in ecosystem service supply-demand balance and flows in a Winter Olympic host region
title_original: Event-driven changes in ecosystem service supply-demand balance and flows in a Winter Olympic host region
summary: Mega-events such as the Olympic Games can drive profound socio-environmental transformations in host regions, but their impacts on ecosystem service supply-demand dynamics and service flows remain poorly understood. This study assesses the spatiotemporal dynamics of four key ecosystem services in Chongli District, China (Beijing, 2022 Winter Olympics venue area), covering the preparation, event, and post-Olympics phases. Results show that the supply-demand ratio for water yield service significantly declined during the event period, followed by gradual recovery in the post-Olympic phase. Conversely, soil conservation and habitat quality services maintain a stable surplus overall. Spatially, the Winter Olympic and residential areas exhibit high demand for water yield and carbon sequestration services, with an increasing trend of supply-demand imbalance. Service flow analysis further reveals that carbon sequestration and habitat quality services primarily transfer from areas with a high supply-demand ratio to regions of intensive human activity, with the Winter Olympic area being the main recipient and showing an increasing service flow intensity. Socioeconomic factors, including population density, nighttime light, and built-up percentage, tend to undermine the supply-demand balance, with this inhibitory impact being especially pronounced within the Winter Olympic area. Moreover, threshold analysis revealed nonlinear driver effects on ecosystem service supply-demand balance. Nighttime light and built-up expansion mainly weakened the balance of water yield and carbon sequestration services, whereas precipitation enhanced water yield balance after crossing a critical level, and increasing population pressure further reduced habitat quality balance. This study supports actionable management, including flow-informed zoning, threshold-based development caps and compensation schemes to maintain water security, carbon sinks and habitat conservation in mega-event host regions.

title: Continuing the Focus on U.S. Medals: Continued Analyses of Biological Sex Representation During the 2024 and 2026 NBC Primetime Olympic Broadcasts
title_original: Continuing the Focus on U.S. Medals: Continued Analyses of Biological Sex Representation During the 2024 and 2026 NBC Primetime Olympic Broadcasts
summary: This report is a continued examination of the agenda that is set by the National Broadcasting Company’s (NBC’s) in its presentation of male and female athletes during the primetime telecasts of the Olympic Games, with a focus on the 2024 Paris Summer Olympic Games and the 2026 Milan-Cortina Winter Olympic Games. Results are presented from content analyses examining the amount of time devoted to each sporting event and which athletes are most often mentioned during the primetime broadcasts. While continuing recent trends showing that women received more screen time in the presentation of their events at both Olympic Games, salience analyses of mentioned athletes showed different results between the Summer and Winter Games despite the competition results favoring women who competed. Specifically, during both the 2024 (52.08%) and 2026 (50.65%) Olympic broadcasts, women received the bulk of the time on camera, though the 2026 result is noteworthy as it is the smallest margin between men’s and women’s Olympic coverage to date. Salience analyses found that women were mentioned more than men during the 2024 Olympic coverage, while the opposite was true for the 2026 Games. This report concludes with a discussion of implications and a look to the future.

title: IMPACT OF SAUNA BATHING ON GENERAL HEALTH - THE LATEST REPORTS
title_original: IMPACT OF SAUNA BATHING ON GENERAL HEALTH - THE LATEST REPORTS
summary: Sauna bathing is becoming increasingly popular nowadays. This activity is traditional to Finnish culture, as well as being widely used in other countries, especially Scandinavian ones. Today, there are different types of sauna, including, for example, the traditional Finnish sauna, Turkish Hammam and the Russian Banya. The aim of this review is to analyse the impact of sauna bathing on various health-related aspects of human life. Many studies show the positive effects of saunas on human health. Regarding the cardiovascular system, sauna bathing causes a decrease in: the risk of death from cardiovascular diseases, the risk of sudden cardiac death, blood pressure, among others. In addition, it has a beneficial effect on arterial stiffness, causes changes in cardiovascular biomarkers, and may reduce the risk of thromboembolic disease and stroke. The positive effect of sauna bathing on the respiratory system is due to the fact that sauna can reduce the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, pneumonia. In addition, sauna has a beneficial effect on the immune system through makers of inflammation. Moreover, sauna has a positive effect on the nervous system, as it reduces the risk of dementia, Alzheimer's disease and psychosis. Recent studies from 2017 indicate that sauna bathing has many health benefits and has positive effects on the cardiovascular, respiratory, immune, nervous systems. However, despite the many benefits of sauna use, one must exercise caution and follow safety precautions. More research is needed to confirm all these relationships.

Today, there are different types of sauna, including, for example, the traditional Finnish sauna, Turkish Hammam and the Russian Banya. The aim of this review is to analyse the impact of sauna bathing on various health-related aspects of human life. Many studies show the positive effects of saunas on human health. Regarding the cardiovascular system, sauna bathing causes a decrease in: the risk of death from cardiovascular diseases, the risk of sudden cardiac death, blood pressure, among others. In addition, it has a beneficial effect on arterial stiffness, causes changes in cardiovascular biomarkers, and may reduce the risk of thromboembolic disease and stroke. The positive effect of sauna bathing on the respiratory system is due to the fact that sauna can reduce the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, pneumonia. In addition, sauna has a beneficial effect on the immune system through makers of inflammation. Moreover, sauna has a positive effect on the nervous system, as it reduces the risk of dementia, Alzheimer's disease and psychosis. Recent studies from 2017 indicate that sauna bathing has many health benefits and has positive effects on the cardiovascular, respiratory, immune, nervous systems. However, despite the many benefits of sauna use, one must exercise caution and follow safety precautions. More research is needed to confirm all these relationships.

title: Finger Joint Capsulitis in Rock Climbers: A Scoping Review of Prevalence and Management Strategies
title_original: Finger Joint Capsulitis in Rock Climbers: A Scoping Review of Prevalence and Management Strategies
summary: Rock climbing and its disciplines have seen a dramatic rise in popularity worldwide, accelerated by the sport's inclusion in the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games (Lutter et al., 2021). As participation increases, the exposure of individuals to common rock climbing injuries has naturally heightened (Forrester et al., 2018). Of the injuries associated with climbing disciplines, hand and digit injuries have been identified as the most common, regardless of level of experience, sex, or discipline (Kovarova et al., 2024; Grønhaug, 2018). As training intensity increases, the prominence of both chronic overuse and acute injuries has continued to grow (Schöffl et al., 2025). No scoping review has been conducted specifically on finger joint capsulitis/synovitis in rock climbers. A recent broad scoping review of musculoskeletal injuries in rock climbing (Vagy et al., 2026) identified inconsistent diagnostic reporting and insufficient diagnostic detail as key limitations of the current literature, recommending future condition-specific evidence synthesis as a priority. Adjacent conditions affecting the DIP/PIP joints have received dedicated scoping reviews (Jaini et al., 2025), yet capsulitis/synovitis in climbers remains unreviewed. This scoping review will be conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological guidance for scoping reviews (Peters et al., 2020). A systematic search will be conducted across PubMed, CINAHL Complete via EBSCOhost, and SPORTDiscus via EBSCOhost, supplemented by grey literature searching. This review has two research questions. The primary research question asks: what is the reported prevalence of finger joint capsulitis/synovitis in rock climbers? The secondary research question asks: what management approaches have been described or evaluated for finger joint capsulitis/synovitis in rock climbers? The expected outcomes of this review are first, the review will provide the first consolidated map of reported prevalence data for this condition across the climbing literature, identifying the range of figures reported, the variation in diagnostic criteria and terminology used, and the populations studied. Second, the review will map the conservative management approaches that have been described or evaluated, identifying the current state of clinical evidence and highlighting where evidence-based guidelines are lacking. Through these outputs, this review aims to inform physiotherapy clinical practice, support the development of future evidence-based management guidelines, and identify priorities for future primary research on this condition.

title: An Alternative Sports Order? A Study of Sino-Russian Olympic Diplomacy
title_original: An Alternative Sports Order? A Study of Sino-Russian Olympic Diplomacy
summary: This chapter examines the evolution of Sino-Russian relations through the lens of Olympic diplomacy, focusing on the diplomatic boycott of the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic Games and Russia’s exclusion from subsequent Olympic competitions. It analyses how China and Russia have engaged with the Olympic arena as a site of geopolitical contestation, highlighting both moments of alignment and differentiation in their respective responses. The analysis situates these two cases within the longer historical evolution of Olympic boycotts and sporting sanctions, comparing Chinese and Russian diplomatic strategies in the face of pressure from Western democracies and international sporting institutions. Drawing on historical contextualisation and analysis of official statements and sport-related initiatives, the chapter explores whether recent developments point toward coordinated efforts and experimentation with alternative sporting formats, thereby illuminating processes of contestation and counter-ordering in the governance of global sport and their implications for the international order.

title: The Finnish Gymnastics and Sport Confederation, 1944–1952
title_original: The Finnish Gymnastics and Sport Confederation, 1944–1952
summary: This study examines the largest sport organisation in Finland, the Finnish Gymnastics and Sport Confederation (Suomen Voimistelu- ja Urheiluliitto, SVUL), and its role in Finnish sport and society between 1944 and 1952. The SVUL had to define and enact the relationship between sport and politics in the transition from the Second World War to the Cold War and adapt to the foreign and domestic political changes that were taking place in Finland, especially during the so-called ‘Years of Peril’ (1944–1948), when a Communist coup seemed imminent. Finland adapted to a pro-Soviet foreign policy as well. However, the SVUL retained its largely conservative patriotic values by sticking strictly to sport, making concessions to the Workers’ Sport Union (Työväen Urheiluliitto) and emphasising that it rejected all politics. The Finnish Grand Games in 1947 gave an opportunity for a safe rebirth of moderate Finnish nationalism, and in 1952 Finland hosted the Olympic Games. Both events were widely seen as symbolic relief and as rehabilitation in world politics and international sport.

title: Characteristics of patients receiving a prescription for adapted physical activity in Aubervilliers: a retrospective study
title_original: Characteristics of patients receiving a prescription for adapted physical activity in Aubervilliers: a retrospective study
summary: physical activity identified in the study was the desire for good mental, physical, and social health¹⁰. Due to its sustainable nature, this program, a pioneer in France since 2015, seemed conducive to studying adherence to an adapted physical activity program.The main objective of the study was to describe the sociodemographic profile of patients benefiting from this program since its creation in 2015. The secondary objective was to compare the profile of patients who received an APA prescription under this program but never attended any session with those who attended multiple sessions.METHOD Study Type and PopulationA retrospective observational study was conducted. The study population consisted of adult patients who consulted at the Aubervilliers CMS and who had received a prescription under the "exercise on prescription" program.The city of Aubervilliers is in Seine-Saint-Denis (93), a department with an over-representation of cardiovascular diseases and social precarity¹¹. The "exercise on prescription" program was created in 2015 at the Aubervilliers CMS in partnership with the municipality. It is free for beneficiaries. Initially, the GP identifies the indication, proposes it to the patient, and prescribes it. The prescribing physicians for APA could be GPs from the CMS and some private GPs in Aubervilliers who were partners in the program. The patient is then registered, and the contact details of the sports educator are provided to them. The sports educator has validated training as a level 2 health-sport animator from the Île-de-France Regional Olympic and Sports Center. They offer an interview during which they assess the patient's functional abilities, then specify the modalities of the APA sessions, with the possibility of attending one or more weekly sessions, with multiple time slots during the week and several activities (yoga, muscle strengthening, aquagym). The number of sessions is not predetermined and depends on the participant. Data Collection Methods All patients who received an APA prescription from a GP practicing at the Aubervilliers CMS since the creation of the program were included in the study, regardless of whether they resided in Aubervilliers. In 2024, the Aubervilliers CMS had 6 full-time equivalent (FTE) GPs. Data collection from consultations between January

title: Sports Policy and National Development: A Comparative Study of India & China
title_original: Sports Policy and National Development: A Comparative Study of India & China
summary: Sports, we now know, are not just a form of entertainment or physical activity; they are also linked to health, education, social inclusion, economic development, youth empowerment and the global identity of a country. Sports are a major part of India and China's national development agendas, yet the sports policies of India and China have a different structure, priority and approach. China has achieved a lot of success in elite competitive sports with a centralized and goal-oriented system. In recent years, India has focused more on the mass movement of sports, talent identification and sports infrastructure, the participation of women and differently-abled athletes, and international excellence. The Khelo Bharat Niti-2025 has been introduced by India on 10 July 2025. It is aimed at a more inclusive sports ecosystem from the grassroots to the Olympic stage. It is all about talent identification, sports science, sports medicine, sports infrastructure, social inclusion and sports as a career. Sports policy is in its first phase in China now with a vision of becoming a "Sports power" nation. China's "Plan for Building a Sports Power during the 15th Five-Year Period," published in 2026, focuses on public health, sports competition quality, sports governance and the development of the sports sector. In this research paper we compare the sports policies of both countries in terms of similarities, differences and achievements, and potential lessons for India.

title: The Politicization of Soviet–Icelandic Sport Relations before the 1980 Moscow Olympics
title_original: The Politicization of Soviet–Icelandic Sport Relations before the 1980 Moscow Olympics
summary: This chapter examines the politicization of Soviet–Icelandic sport relations prior to the 1980 Moscow Olympic Games, focusing on the bilateral sport agreement signed in 1978. It argues that the Soviet initiative formed part of a broader nation-branding strategy linked to the Olympics and the cultural Cold War, through which sport functioned as a tool of soft power. The chapter also analyses the domestic impact of the agreement, highlighting tensions between the Icelandic government and the national sport movement. Despite their formal autonomy, Icelandic sport organizations were excluded from the negotiation process, prompting criticism and raising questions about the relationship between state authorities and non-governmental actors. Finally, the chapter considers whether the agreement influenced Iceland’s decision to participate in the Moscow Olympics despite international boycott pressures. Although no direct link can be established, the case illustrates how a small state navigated geopolitical tensions during the Cold War and underscores the political significance of sport in international relations.

title: Cyber trends in sport as a new environment for guided human development
title_original: Cyber trends in sport as a new environment for guided human development
summary: Relevance. Cyber trends in sport are considered as a manifestation of an anthropotechnological shift in which sports activity is organised within a single circuit of interaction between the brain, the body, the digital environment and management systems. Digitalisation develops along two lines: as a means of managing preparation, monitoring the functional state and analysing competitive activity, and as a source of new lines of practice – virtual and simulated disciplines, esports, phygital and operator disciplines, as well as adaptive and rehabilitation applications of digital technologies. Objective. To examine cyber trends in sport as digital and hybrid environments for guided human development, to identify the main types of cyber-sport practices, to describe the types of activity subject they actualise, and to define the tasks of medical-biological and psychophysiological support. Methods. A conceptual comparative review of the Olympic line of virtual and simulated disciplines, esports, phygital and operator disciplines, and adaptive and rehabilitation applications of digital technologies. It employs analysis of literature on sports psychophysiology, sports medicine and esports research, analysis of International Olympic Committee documents and Russian regulatory acts, and a comparative analysis of environments by the type of activity subject they form and their functional demands. Results. It is proposed to distinguish virtual sports, simulated sports and esports as different anthropotechnical environments that differ in the structure of bodily action, cognitive and sensorimotor load and the way the result is formed. Traditional sports develop a bodily-motor athlete; digital replicas of classical disciplines – one acting in a virtual or simulation model; esports – a cognitive-interface competitive subject; phygital disciplines – a cyberphysical athlete; and operator disciplines – an athlete-operator working through a technical interface under conditions of high speed and uncertainty. The support of such environments should include assessment of the functional state, cognitive load, stress, sleep, visual fatigue and recovery. Conclusion. Cyber trends reflect a transition from sport as a predominantly bodily-motor practice to a spectrum of digital and hybrid anthropotechnical environments in which the result is determined by a combination of physical, cognitive, sensorimotor and interface components of activity. This potential is realised only with scientifically grounded support: control of load, recovery, sleep and visual fatigue, and prevention of problematic gaming behaviour.

title: Disclosure, Concealment, and Accountable Testimony: A 20-Year Comparative Textual Analysis of Islamic Moral Reasoning in a Muslim Athlete's Autoethnographies
title_original: Disclosure, Concealment, and Accountable Testimony: A 20-Year Comparative Textual Analysis of Islamic Moral Reasoning in a Muslim Athlete's Autoethnographies
summary: Autoethnography can connect embodied experience to the social organisation of sport, but writing the self also exposes relationships, institutions, and other people. Relational ethics addresses this problem, yet sport scholarship has given comparatively less attention to the explicit moral traditions through which authors decide both what to disclose and what to withhold. This article conducts a critical autoethnographic textual comparison of two works written twenty years apart. The first is a 2006 doctoral study of power, coercion, injury, and the coach-athlete relationship. The second is a 2026 book that locates sporting development within a broader life history and the Maldives’ inaugural Olympic participation. 16 focal representational decisions were analysed through a comparison matrix and five situated Islamic concepts: amanah (trust), 'adl (justice), niyyah (intention), satr (protective concealment), and hisab (accountability). The comparison shows a shift from an individuated pseudonym carrying diary-derived speech towards named individuals, selective paraphrase, recurrent retrospective self-correction, and wider structural framing. Both texts declare reconstruction rather than transcription, so what changes across the twenty years is the unit of representation rather than the evidential claim. From this analysis, the article develops accountable testimony: a non-mechanical approach that places a burden of justification on silence as well as disclosure. It contributes to autoethnographic ethics and athlete safeguarding by showing how faith-informed moral reasoning can be made methodologically explicit, proportionate, and open to scholarly scrutiny.

title: The Development Challenges of English Sevens Rugby in China: A Multidimensional Analysis Based on the Project's Essential Attributes
title_original: The Development Challenges of English Sevens Rugby in China: A Multidimensional Analysis Based on the Project's Essential Attributes
summary: Since becoming an official Olympic event in 2009, seven-a-side rugby has achieved unprecedented development opportunities worldwide. As a staunch executor of Olympic strategy, China has invested substantial resources in this sport, with the women's team securing a historic sixth-place finish at the Paris Olympics. However, this achievement has not altered the fundamental landscape of seven-a-side rugby being a "niche sport" in China. This paper constructs a three-dimensional analytical framework-"sporting characteristics-system compatibility-cultural soil"-based on the intrinsic attributes of seven-a-side rugby to systematically examine the deep-seated challenges in its development within China. Research reveals a structural mismatch between the sport's high-intensity, fast-paced, and high-contact nature and China's state-led talent cultivation model in competitive sports. Its Western-originated, physically confrontational cultural DNA also creates a cognitive gap with traditional Chinese body concepts and athletic aesthetics. Additionally, its reliance on campus promotion and grassroots club development conflicts with China's institutional inertia of concentrating sports resources in Olympic-dominant events. The convergence of these three tensions forms the structural root cause behind seven-a-side rugby's "over a decade post-Olympic inclusion yet still struggling for widespread adoption" in China. The study proposes that overcoming this predicament requires transcending the "Olympic-driven" singular development logic, returning to the sport's intrinsic attributes, and establishing a tripartite collaborative development path encompassing "campus promotion-social engagement-elite competition."

title: Biomechanics of the Snatch and Clean and Jerk in Olympic Weightlifting: A Systematic Review
title_original: Biomechanics of the Snatch and Clean and Jerk in Olympic Weightlifting: A Systematic Review
summary: Biomechanical studies of the Olympic snatch and clean and jerk use heterogeneous samples and measurement protocols. This systematic review summarizes measurement approaches, technical findings, lift-specific coverage, and sex representation. Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed and Scopus were searched on 20 September 2026, retaining publications first available by 30 June 2026. The exports contained 241, 151 and 264 records (656 in total); 314 duplicate entries were removed, leaving 342 distinct database records. The authors confirmed full-text assessment of the previously assembled evidence set. Of its 74 publications, one narrative review (Bartonietz, 1996) was reclassified as contextual rather than original research, leaving 73 primary publications. Fifty-two of the original 74 entries matched the new electronic exports by DOI or title; 21 additional primary publications were retained from the authors’ previously assembled reference set. Among the 73 primary publications, 45 examined the snatch only, 15 examined clean/jerk movements without snatch data, and 13 examined both categories; 23 included female athletes. Eight publications are cited only for methodological or contextual interpretation. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. The review highlights the uneven coverage of the competition lifts, limited female representation and need for comparable, field-validated multimodal measurements. No prospective review protocol was registered.

title: A Snow Sports Venue Low-Carbon Evaluation System Based on Life-Cycle Carbon Emissions
title_original: A Snow Sports Venue Low-Carbon Evaluation System Based on Life-Cycle Carbon Emissions
summary: Large-scale snow sports venues are characterized by unique terrain, seasonal operation modes, and long service lifespan. Consequently, a comprehensive assessment method is required to account for both life-cycle carbon emissions and multi-dimensional low-carbon performance. This study proposes a Sports Venue Low-carbon Evaluation System (SV-LCES) that integrates life-cycle carbon emission evaluation (LCCE) with multidimensional performance assessment. Using engineering inventories, EnergyPlus simulations, and emission factor methods, a life-cycle carbon emission model was developed and applied to the National Sliding Centre (NSC) and Yanqing Winter Olympic Village (YWOV), with the latter constructed as a supporting venue for the NSC. Carbon hotspots were identified, and an evaluation system was established through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and LCCE combined weighting and grey clustering. The results show that the operation and maintenance stage was the dominant contributor to the life-cycle carbon emissions, accounting for 56.39% of the total. The calculated carbon emission reduction rates of the NSC and YWOV were 40.17% and 46.37%, respectively, indicating a relatively small difference. However, after the low-carbon performance of the venues was comprehensively evaluated, SV-LCES distinguished their performance levels as Grade B for NSC and Grade A for YWOV. The proposed framework offers a holistic approach to low-carbon evaluation of large-scale sports venues and other energy-intensive public buildings.

title: The 1980 Moscow Olympics Boycott
title_original: The 1980 Moscow Olympics Boycott
summary: When the United States government, following the Soviet Union’s invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979, initiated an international boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics, most of the national Olympic committees in Europe did not join Carter’s initiative. However, due to pressure from their respective governments, some of them did. Norway was an exception, as the country’s most important sports bodies chose to boycott the 1980 Olympics without any apparent pressure from the government. This chapter analyses, in a comparative manner, why Norway and Sweden (which chose to participate) reached different conclusions. Norway’s NATO-membership was only part of the explanation. Even more important was that there was a higher degree of institutional stability in Sweden than in Norway and, above all, that the Post-War heroic culture of remembrance from the Second World War influenced the decision to join the boycott in Norway.

title: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
title_original: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
summary: BACKGROUND: Athletes commonly implement post-exercise cold-water immersion (CWI), with several meta-analyses having assessed its effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To thoroughly review, appraise, and summarise existing systematic reviews with meta-analyses (SRMA) examining the effects of post-exercise CWI on the recovery of exercise performance and adaptation. METHODS: An umbrella review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. PROSPERO registration: (CRD420251103267). Eight databases were searched, including Web of Science, Scopus, SPORTDiscus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Embase, MEDLINE, and PubMed. Systematic reviews with meta-analyses of peer-reviewed randomised controlled trials examining post-exercise CWI vs passive rest or other recovery modalities on performance, training adaptation, or physiological, biochemical, and perceptual outcomes in healthy humans were included, with restriction to the English language. RESULTS: Fifteen SRMAs published between 2011 and 2025, comprising 161 unique studies, were included. Overall methodological quality was low to critically low, and certainty of evidence was low to very low, mainly due to inconsistency and imprecision. Protocols of 10-15 min at 10-15 or 5-10 °C appear to be most effective for improving performance and recovery. Post-exercise CWI resulted in significant improvements in muscular power at 24 h post-high-intensity exercise and at 24-48 h post-eccentric exercise, and in jump performance at 24-48 h, despite impaired jump performance in the initial hours after post-exercise CWI. Endurance performance improved immediately after CWI, but CWI produced no later benefits or positive effects on adaptations. CWI did not improve muscular strength performance, and impaired strength and hypertrophic gains. CWI improved heart rate variability immediately after exercise, reduced muscle soreness up to 96 h, and lowered creatine kinase (CK) concentrations between 24 and 72 h, with no significant effects on C-reactive protein or interleukin-6 up to 72 h. No immediate impact on blood lactate or lactate dehydrogenase was found, although some reductions appear 24-72 h post-exercise. CONCLUSIONS: Post-exercise CWI confers outcome-specific recovery benefits but may impair resistance training adaptations with chronic use. These findings support a periodised, context-driven approach to CWI implementation rather than routine application after all exercise sessions.

title: Sporting Ambitions, Geopolitical Goals
title_original: Sporting Ambitions, Geopolitical Goals
summary: This chapter will cover Morocco’s engagement with international sport. The focus will be on how this country leverages sports events to advance its geopolitical, economic and cultural objectives. Morocco showcases its organisational capabilities and infrastructure by hosting prestigious events at the regional and global level, positioning itself as a relevant player in global sports governance. In particular, football serves as a cornerstone of Morocco’s sports diplomacy, highlighting its role as co-host (alongside Spain and Portugal) of the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup, its historic fourth place in 2022 and the men’s bronze medal in the Paris 2024 Olympics. These achievements, together with the development of scouting processes leading to the naturalisation of athletes from the diasporas, have amplified the national pride and elevated the country’s global visibility. A challenge for Moroccan sports diplomacy is the management of internal, regional and international political tensions, especially concerning Western Sahara, which has caused some sporting incidents with Algeria and Spain. Therefore, Morocco illuminates how African nations can globally use sports as a tool for soft power, geopolitical manoeuvring and the assertion of national identity.

title: Danish Sport Politics during the Cold War
title_original: Danish Sport Politics during the Cold War
summary: This chapter begins with an analysis of how the Danish Sports Federation responded to the Soviet Union’s crushing of the revolt in Hungary in 1956 and, just once, broke with the tradition not to mix sport and politics. After that, the article studies the beginning of sports cooperation between Denmark and the Soviet Union from 1963 until the ‘Prague Spring’ in 1968. The focus of the article is on how the Danish Sports Federation, the Danish Olympic Committee, the Danish press, the Danish Parliament and the Danish government responded to the boycott discussions connected to the Olympic Games in Moscow 1980. The article also comments on the Olympic Games in Los Angeles 1984 and the problems connected to some Danish participants who were members of the organization ‘Sports for Peace’.

title: Surveillance of Athletes’ Health in Resource-Constrained African Sports Contexts: Why Context Matters and Time To Catch Up
title_original: Surveillance of Athletes’ Health in Resource-Constrained African Sports Contexts: Why Context Matters and Time To Catch Up
summary: Athlete health surveillance is fundamental to understanding, preventing, and managing injuries, illnesses, and other health problems in sport. While standardized surveillance systems developed by organizations such as the International Olympic Committee (IOC) have substantially advanced sports medicine globally, their applicability across diverse African sporting environments remains insufficiently examined. Many existing surveillance approaches assume the availability of trained medical personnel, robust health infrastructure, standardized documentation systems, and stable sporting environments—conditions that are not readily accessible across Africa. The continent is not homogeneous; some countries and elite sporting programs have surveillance capacities comparable to international standards, while many others operate under significant resource constraints. This commentary aims to examine the limitations of conventional athlete health surveillance approaches in African settings and to advocate for context-sensitive, African-led surveillance systems capable of generating locally relevant evidence to inform injury prevention, health policy, and athlete welfare. Leveraging collaborations among African researchers, clinicians, universities, sports federations, healthcare organizations, and international partners offers an opportunity to develop sustainable surveillance systems while strengthening research and clinical capacity across the continent.

title: Gender eligibility regulations in international federations after 2022: Accommodation, transformation, and exclusion
title_original: Gender eligibility regulations in international federations after 2022: Accommodation, transformation, and exclusion
summary: In 2021, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) introduced the Framework on Fairness, Inclusion, and Non-Discrimination on the Basis of Gender Identity and Sex Variations, inviting international federations (IFs) to develop their own sport-specific competition policies for trans and Differences in Sex Development athletes. This article analyses the adoption of its 10 principles across 10 IFs, assessing whether the policies support transformative approaches to gender diversity in competitive sports. The findings show that IFs largely continue to reinforce restrictive norms, emphasizing testosterone thresholds while neglecting broader inclusivity. The analysed regulations rely on contested science, impose medical surveillance, and discriminate against affected athletes. The study highlights how the 2021 IOC Framework, despite its progressive rhetoric, failed to provide substantive guidance, thereby enabling IFs to actively produce exclusion by unknowing: ignoring readily available knowledge about gender diversity in elite sport.

title: French Sports Diplomacy and Soft Power Acquisition
title_original: French Sports Diplomacy and Soft Power Acquisition
summary: This chapter examines the trajectory and future of French sports diplomacy in the wake of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games. While the Games were widely acclaimed as a success, they also signalled the end of a political and diplomatic cycle in which mega-events served as the cornerstone of France&s;s international influence. This raises a central question: does France possess a coherent and durable sport diplomacy, or has it relied primarily on the opportunistic use of major events to project its image abroad? The chapter traces the institutionalisation of sports diplomacy in France since the early 2010s, through initiatives such as the appointment of a Sport Ambassador and the creation of interministerial structures. It highlights notable achievements—including the Paris 2024 bid, greater French representation in international federations, and the global recognition of organisational expertise—while underscoring enduring structural, political, and conjunctural limitations. The analysis ultimately argues that the future of French sports diplomacy will depend on its ability to move beyond an event-driven approach and to articulate a sustainable, strategically integrated vision of sport as an instrument of foreign policy.

title: Stable technical profile despite increasing technical diversity across the last three Olympic cycles in elite female extra-lightweight judo
title_original: Stable technical profile despite increasing technical diversity across the last three Olympic cycles in elite female extra-lightweight judo
summary: Objective: To analyze the technical-tactical behavior and scoring effectiveness of techniques in elite female extra-lightweight (≤48 kg) judo across the last three Olympic cycles (2016, 2020, and 2024). Methods: A retrospective observational study which analyzed 159 official International Judo Federation World Circuit contests (53 per cycle) involving athletes ranked among the top 20 in the World Ranking. A total of 107 scoring techniques were identified according to the Kodokan classification and the official IJF rules applicable to each Olympic cycle. Results: No significant differences were observed in the distribution of technical groups across Olympic cycles (χ²=3.109, p=0.927; Cramér's V=0.121). Likewise, the distribution of techniques resulting in Ippon (χ²=3.637, p=0.888) and Waza-ari (χ²=6.383, p=0.604) remained stable. Although the overall technical profile was preserved, the diversity of individual scoring techniques increased from 17 techniques in the 2016 Olympic cycle to 24 in the 2020 cycle, and remained high in 2024 (23 techniques). Sode-tsuri-komi-goshi predominated in 2016, whereas Ouchi-gari became the most frequent scoring technique in 2020 and remained among the leading techniques in 2024. Katame-waza consistently produced most Ippon, whereas Ashi-waza and Te-waza remained the principal sources of Waza-ari. Conclusions: Despite successive IJF rule modifications, the technical profile of elite female extra-lightweight judo remained remarkably stable across the last three Olympic cycles. Elite athletes expanded their technical repertoire while maintaining the effectiveness of the principal scoring strategies, providing coaches with evidence to optimize weight category-specific technical and tactical training.

title: The Impact of Paralympic and Olympic Broadcasts on Viewer Engagement: The Role of Television in Shaping Staycation Trends in India
title_original: The Impact of Paralympic and Olympic Broadcasts on Viewer Engagement: The Role of Television in Shaping Staycation Trends in India
summary: Sports broadcasting's impact on viewer engagement is a multifaceted topic that encompasses factors such as viewer preferences, audience carryover, social media participation, and the effects of in-the-moment events and nation-related values on viewer attention. The way the Olympic and Paralympic Games are televised shapes attitudes and perceptions of athletes and people with disabilities, with substantial effects on spectator engagement. The 2020 Tokyo Games, as well as the 2024 Paris Games, broke all broadcast viewership records for the number of broadcasters, viewers, and live events. It was hailed as noteworthy for its massive media coverage, which helped promote the disability athletic movement. Through passionate narrative, Paralympic broadcasts run the risk of perpetuating stereotypes, even though they can also encourage empathy and social transformation. Viewers' perceptions of the credibility and athleticism of Paralympic sports compared to Olympic sports are influenced by how these events are portrayed. Distinct categories of sports enthusiasts include information searchers, entertainment seekers, common spectators, and ardent supporters. In contrast to comedies or dramas, sports programs are mostly chosen by ardent fans and have less of an impact on broader audiences. All things considered, the media is extremely important in either supporting or contradicting society norms and prejudices towards disability and sports.

title: National Pride vs. Global Unity: Exploring Nationalism-Infused CSR and Stakeholder Perceptions in Global Sports Events
title_original: National Pride vs. Global Unity: Exploring Nationalism-Infused CSR and Stakeholder Perceptions in Global Sports Events
summary: Abstract Global sporting events, such as the Olympics, often highlight a delicate tension between universal ideals of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and nationalistic appeals to local pride. Against this backdrop, the present study investigates how moral foundations (fairness vs. loyalty) and national attachment shape stakeholder perceptions of nationalism-infused CSR motives and CSR authenticity. Building on moral foundation theory and attribution-based CSR research, we tested hypotheses regarding the interplay between these variables. Conducting a survey (N = 755) through Dynata, we found that fairness-oriented individuals attributed egoistic- and strategic-driven motives, while people with in-group/loyalty foundation perceived value-driven motives from the initiatives.

title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Injury Mechanisms of Taekwondo-Related Injuries: A Systematic Review
title_original: Epidemiological Characteristics and Injury Mechanisms of Taekwondo-Related Injuries: A Systematic Review
summary: As a highly-combative Olympic sport, taekwondo has one of the highest injury-incidence rates among Olympic disciplines, yet its epidemiological characteristics and injury patterns remain unclear. This study performed the-first-ever systematic analysis of the epidemiological features and injury mechanisms of taekwondo. A systematic search identified 552 publications published between 2000 and 2024, among which 24 studies covering 15,170 athletes met the inclusion criteria. Results demonstrated that lower-extremity injuries accounted for the largest proportion (54.3%), with the ankle/foot, knee and face being the most-frequently injured sites. Contusions, sprains and strains were the predominant injury types. The injury risk was markedly higher in the third round than in the first two rounds, while the first round carried the lowest risk, a trend associated with fatigue accumulation and aggressive tactics. Major contributing factors to injuries included inattention, unsatisfactory venue facilities, improper use of protective equipment, rule revisions, high-difficulty techniques and insufficient physical conditioning. It is recommended to implement the International Olympic Committee Injury Surveillance System (IOC-ISS) for standardized injury monitoring, together with improvements in protective-gear technology and rule optimization. Future research should prioritize biomechanical analysis of taekwondo movements, long‑term follow-up of chronic injuries, and the establishment of an integrated system combining prevention, surveillance and rehabilitation.

title: Individualization of training load in Paralympic powerlifting based on nosology
title_original: Individualization of training load in Paralympic powerlifting based on nosology
summary: The purpose of the study is to substantiate the necessity of individualizing training loads in Paralympic powerlifting, taking into account the nosological characteristics of athletes. Research methods: theoretical analysis of scientific and methodological literature. Research results and conclusions. Nosological groups were identified taking into account physiological and biomechanical characteristics. The features of planning training loads for each nosological group were determined: control of autonomic reactions, emphasis on the development of the triceps brachii and speed training without the use of fixing belts for athletes with spinal cord injuries; individualization of the "load–velocity" relationship for short-statured athletes and the use of wrist wraps; priority development of the abdominal and back muscles in athletes with amputations; as well as analysis of barbell kinematic characteristics and the predominance of speed training for athletes with manifestations of hypertonia, ataxia, and athetosis. For each nosological group, features were identified that can be taken into account when planning training loads, which can improve the efficiency and safety of the training process in Paralympic powerlifting.

The features of planning training loads for each nosological group were determined: control of autonomic reactions, emphasis on the development of the triceps brachii and speed training without the use of fixing belts for athletes with spinal cord injuries; individualization of the "load–velocity" relationship for short-statured athletes and the use of wrist wraps; priority development of the abdominal and back muscles in athletes with amputations; as well as analysis of barbell kinematic characteristics and the predominance of speed training for athletes with manifestations of hypertonia, ataxia, and athetosis. For each nosological group, features were identified that can be taken into account when planning training loads, which can improve the efficiency and safety of the training process in Paralympic powerlifting.

title: Sponsors’ health-related messaging & corporate social responsibility: a multi country analysis of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games
title_original: Sponsors’ health-related messaging & corporate social responsibility: a multi country analysis of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games
summary: Research Aim: This paper extends Furtado et al. (2025)’s exploration of health-related messaging before and during the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games. Given that the overwhelming majority (95%) of that study’s health-related messages emanated from corporations, this paper aims to explore the confluence of health messaging with sport mega event (SME) sponsorship and corporate social responsibility (CSR). More specifically, this paper aims to categorise the types of health messaging and activations by national and transnational sponsors accredited through individual National Olympic Committees (NOC) and The Olympic Partner (TOP) programme. Our focus on health adds original contributions to the extant literature on leveraging sport sponsorship as a strategic component of CSR (McCullough and Trail, 2023; Uhrich et al., 2014).

title: Public Perceptions of Disability and Para Athletes Before and After the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games: An Exploratory Independent-Samples Study
title_original: Public Perceptions of Disability and Para Athletes Before and After the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games: An Exploratory Independent-Samples Study
summary: The Paralympic Games are frequently promoted as a catalyst for social change, yet evidence regarding their social legacy remains limited and inconclusive. This study examined differences in French public perceptions of disability before and after the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games using an independent-samples pre–post design. Two surveys were administered to French adults one month before the Games (Time 1: n = 948; Mage = 36.43 years, SD = 13.67) and approximately two months after the Games (Time 2: n = 930; Mage = 37.40 years, SD = 11.83). The questionnaire assessed general perceptions of disability, perceptions of Para athletes, perceived sporting and professional capabilities of persons with physical and vision impairments, and perceived improvements in public accessibility. Participants surveyed after the Games reported higher scores on general disability perceptions, perceptions of Para athletes, and perceptions of persons with physical disabilities. In contrast, lower scores were observed on four of five items concerning persons with vision impairments. Participants with a disability and those with a close personal connection to disability also reported more positive perceptions of public accessibility after the Games. These findings suggest that public perceptions differed before and after the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games but varied by disability type. Given the independent-samples design, they should be interpreted cautiously.

title: From outputs to outcomes? Examining the evolution of social impact reporting in UK major sport events [Abstract]
title_original: From outputs to outcomes? Examining the evolution of social impact reporting in UK major sport events [Abstract]
summary: Aim and Research Questions This research examines how social impact claims and reporting practices are constructed, evidenced, and evolved within documentary materials relating to major sport events in the UK across four cycles aligned to the Rio (2013 - 2016), Tokyo (2017 - 2021), Paris (2022 - 2024), and Los Angeles (2025 - present) Olympic and Paralympic Games. It asks: 1. How are social impact claims constructed and evidenced within major sport event reporting across the four cycles? 2. What content trends and changes occur across cycles? The project frames these questions as an opportunity to demonstrate how a Theory of Change (ToC) approach can strengthen evidential claims, support longitudinal assessment, and encourage more policy relevant, equitable reporting.

title: Paralympic sport in Central Asia: a scoping review with descriptive analysis of participation, achievement, and medal efficiency (1996–2024)
title_original: Paralympic sport in Central Asia: a scoping review with descriptive analysis of participation, achievement, and medal efficiency (1996–2024)
summary: Published research on Paralympic sport in Central Asia remains limited despite the region's growing presence at the Games. This review focuses on elite, Games-level participation and achievement. We conducted a scoping review reported in line with the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, alongside an analysis of International Paralympic Committee (IPC) archival data for five Central Asian countries (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan) across Summer (1996–2024) and Winter (1994–2026) Games, framed through the SPLISS model and the constraint-led approach. The scoping review maps international knowledge; the IPC analysis documents regional outcomes, offering complementary evidence. The review identified three domains: income-, gender-, and technology-linked participation gaps (D1); discipline-specific age profiles ranging from a median of 25 years in Para Swimming to 38 years in Para Equestrian (D2); and ten national policy factors linked to Paralympic success (D3). IPC data showed Central Asian participation rising from 15 athletes in 1996 to 113 in 2024, led by Uzbekistan ( n = 64, Paris 2024) and Kazakhstan ( n = 44), concentrated in Para Athletics, Para Judo, and Para Powerlifting, plus a full Kazakhstani sitting volleyball squad and Para Swimming. Female representation rose from 0% in 1996 to 41.6% in 2024, near the ∼43% global benchmark. Medal efficiency was 0% before 2012, spiked to 73.5% at Rio 2016 (95% CI 59.7%–83.8%), driven by Uzbekistan winning more medals than athletes that edition, then settled at 32.9% (Tokyo 2020) and 31.0% (Paris 2024, 95% CI 23.2%–40.0%); the 2016 spike is statistically distinguishable from other editions, while Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 are not. Uzbekistan grew from 0 athletes in 1996 to 64 in 2024, with the sharpest rise from 32 (Rio 2016) to 64 (Paris 2024), coinciding with documented 2019–2024 state Paralympic-development measures-a plausible institutional account alongside classification reform and host-proximity effects. No study identified by our search has examined elite Paralympic sport development in Central Asia specifically. Four research priorities are proposed: epidemiological profiling, adapted policy analysis with regional researchers, longitudinal athlete tracking, and psychological support programs.

title: Historical and Contemporary Functions of Rituals in the Olympic Games
title_original: Historical and Contemporary Functions of Rituals in the Olympic Games
summary: The Olympic Games represent a multidimensional structure in which rituals, symbols, and ceremonial practices occupy an important place alongside athletic competition. In the Ancient Olympic Games, sacred processions, oaths, offerings, sacrifices, and award practices constituted important elements of the religious and social order. In the Modern Olympic Games, the Olympic rings, the flame and torch relay, the oath, and the opening, closing, and medal ceremonies are among the fundamental components of the symbolic and institutional structure of the Olympic Movement. This study aims to evaluate the rituals associated with the Olympic Games in terms of the functions they perform within the Games, rather than limiting the discussion to their historical development or to formal similarities and differences between the Ancient and Modern Olympics. Designed as a narrative review, the study examines historical and classical sources, academic studies, and institutional documents of the International Olympic Committee. Based on the evaluation of the literature, the functions of Olympic rituals were examined under five interrelated dimensions: the production of sacredness and meaning; regulatory, normative, and institutional functions; the formation of unity and belonging; the ritualization of achievement and honor; and the representation and visibility of Olympic values. The findings indicate that, in the Ancient Olympic Games, rituals contributed to maintaining the sacred order, reinforcing behavioral norms, and publicly honoring athletic achievement, whereas in the Modern Olympic Games they serve to sustain institutional order, symbolically reinforce a shared sense of belonging, ceremonially recognize achievement, and make Olympic values visible. In conclusion, Olympic rituals can be regarded not merely as ceremonial elements accompanying the Olympic Games, but as interrelated and multifunctional practices that contribute to the construction and maintenance of the Games’ worlds of meaning, order, belonging, achievement, and values.

title: Sex Differences in Injury, Stoppage and Concussion Rates in Amateur and Olympic-Style Boxing
title_original: Sex Differences in Injury, Stoppage and Concussion Rates in Amateur and Olympic-Style Boxing
summary: Background. Women have boxed at the Olympic Games since 2012; since 2013 elite men have competed without headguards while women have kept them. Sex differences in injury, stoppage and concussion rates in amateur and Olympic-style boxing have not been systematically reviewed. The review question was: in amateur and Olympic-style boxers, do injury incidence, stoppage rates and concussion rates differ between women and men? Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE and Consensus were searched on 29 September 2026 (English-language reports, no date limit), with backward citation searching. Eligible studies reported at least one outcome (injury, stoppage, diagnosed concussion, laceration, fracture, other craniofacial or regional injury, or acute neurocognitive change) for women and men from the same amateur or Olympic-style boxing population with sex-specific denominators; outcomes were kept separate. Screening and extraction were single-reviewer with verification. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty with GRADE. Risk ratios (women versus men) were pooled with a restricted maximum likelihood random-effects model with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Results. From 416 unique database records and 36 citation-search records, four studies were eligible, all International Olympic Committee injury-surveillance cohorts (Olympic Games 2012, 2016 and 2020; Youth Olympic Games 2018). Sex-specific boxing data were available from the published text of two. At London 2012, where both sexes wore headguards, 7 of 36 women (19.4%) and 18 of 247 men (7.3%) sustained a medical-attention injury (risk ratio 2.67, 95% CI 1.20 to 5.94). At Tokyo 2020, where men boxed without headguards and women with them, the reported risk ratio was 0.43 (0.24 to 0.75). The pooled estimate (risk ratio 1.05) was not interpretable (I² = 92%; Hartung-Knapp 95% CI 0.00 to >1000). No eligible study reported stoppages, diagnosed concussion, lacerations, fractures or neurocognitive change by sex. Certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions. The direction of the sex difference in injury reversed once protective-equipment rules diverged by sex, and no sex-stratified evidence exists for stoppages or concussion. Regulators cannot assume equal or unequal risk by sex. Sex-stratified surveillance with exposure denominators, recording stoppage and concussion by sex, is a prerequisite for evidence-based sex-specific rules. Registration. Not registered.

Sex differences in injury, stoppage and concussion rates in amateur and Olympic-style boxing have not been systematically reviewed. The review question was: in amateur and Olympic-style boxers, do injury incidence, stoppage rates and concussion rates differ between women and men? Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE and Consensus were searched on 29 September 2026 (English-language reports, no date limit), with backward citation searching. Eligible studies reported at least one outcome (injury, stoppage, diagnosed concussion, laceration, fracture, other craniofacial or regional injury, or acute neurocognitive change) for women and men from the same amateur or Olympic-style boxing population with sex-specific denominators; outcomes were kept separate. Screening and extraction were single-reviewer with verification. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty with GRADE. Risk ratios (women versus men) were pooled with a restricted maximum likelihood random-effects model with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Results. From 416 unique database records and 36 citation-search records, four studies were eligible, all International Olympic Committee injury-surveillance cohorts (Olympic Games 2012, 2016 and 2020; Youth Olympic Games 2018). Sex-specific boxing data were available from the published text of two. At London 2012, where both sexes wore headguards, 7 of 36 women (19.4%) and 18 of 247 men (7.3%) sustained a medical-attention injury (risk ratio 2.67, 95% CI 1.20 to 5.94). At Tokyo 2020, where men boxed without headguards and women with them, the reported risk ratio was 0.43 (0.24 to 0.75). The pooled estimate (risk ratio 1.05) was not interpretable (I² = 92%; Hartung-Knapp 95% CI 0.00 to >1000). No eligible study reported stoppages, diagnosed concussion, lacerations, fractures or neurocognitive change by sex. Certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions. The direction of the sex difference in injury reversed once protective-equipment rules diverged by sex, and no sex-stratified evidence exists for stoppages or concussion. Regulators cannot assume equal or unequal risk by sex. Sex-stratified surveillance with exposure denominators, recording stoppage and concussion by sex, is a prerequisite for evidence-based sex-specific rules. Registration. Not registered.

title: Introduction: Rivalry, Recognition, and Soft Power in Sport Diplomacy
title_original: Introduction: Rivalry, Recognition, and Soft Power in Sport Diplomacy
summary: Sport diplomacy scholarship has continued to grow in recent years. This new literature builds on earlier ideas but moves beyond the studies as a battle between superpowers or the hosting of mega-events. Moving beyond these countries to consider regional rivalries, minority or oppressed groups, and middle powers brings greater insight into sport diplomacy and how it has functioned, particularly as a form of soft power. The Olympic movement and football are still important within sport diplomacy, but their examination from states other than the dominant countries provides more nuanced understanding. In addition, newer sport diplomacy scholarship incorporates different countries and sports, and increasingly considers women athletes and teams as important actors within sport diplomacy.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Crowds and Disasters: A Vosviewer-Based Study Using the Scopus Database
title_original: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Crowds and Disasters: A Vosviewer-Based Study Using the Scopus Database
summary: Crowds are defined as situations in which large numbers of individuals congregate in close proximity. These environments can be observed in everyday settings such as shopping malls and metro stations, as well as planned events like football matches and the Olympic Games. In such settings, physical closeness, lack of social distancing and insufficient hygiene may pose significant public health and safety risks. When not properly managed, crowds can harm large numbers of people and exacerbate the impacts of existing disasters. The relationship between crowds and disasters is critical to risk assessment and crisis management. This study aims to conduct a bibliometric analysis of research within the context of crowds and disasters by examining documents indexed in the Scopus database using the keywords “crowd and disaster”. Bibliometric visualizations were generated using VOSviewer software. The analysis revealed that the most frequently used keywords were disaster management, crowd disasters, crowdsourcing, social media, and disaster response. In more recent years, keywords such as metro station, crowd evacuation, emergency evacuation, crowd disasters and stampede have gained prominence. It was also found that studies in this area spanned multiple disciplines, notably computer science, engineering, and the social sciences. Based on the findings, three research recommendations are proposed: fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, enhancing international cooperation and promoting research on crowds and disasters.

title: Age-Related Performance in Taekwondo Athletes with Physical Disabilities: An Analysis of the Paralympic Games
title_original: Age-Related Performance in Taekwondo Athletes with Physical Disabilities: An Analysis of the Paralympic Games
summary: Abstract This study investigated age-related performance in Para taekwondo athletes across two Paralympic Games editions, Tokyo 2020 + 1 and Paris 2024, examining potential differences according to Paralympic edition, sex, and competitive achievement. Data were obtained from the official results books of the Paralympic Games and included 192 Paralympic participation records, comprising 95 female and 97 male records. Age-related performance was analyzed according to Paralympic edition, sex, and competitive achievement, classified as medallist or non-medallist. Mann–Whitney U tests were used to compare age differences between groups, while chi-square (χ²) tests of independence were applied to examine the distribution of athletes across age categories (≤ 20, 21–25, 26–30, and ≥ 31 years). Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Female athletes were younger than male athletes at Paralympic participation (26 vs. 28 years; U = 3765.00, p = 0.028). No significant differences were observed between Paralympic editions (27 years for both; U = 4128.50, p = 0.653) or between medallists and non-medallists (26 vs. 28 years; U = 3395.50, p = 0.053). The distribution of athletes across age groups was similar for both sexes (χ²(3) = 5.71, p = 0.126) and competitive achievement levels (χ²(3) = 4.89, p = 0.180). Age differed by sex, whereas no significant age differences were observed according to competitive achievement or Paralympic edition. Overall, the age profile of Para taekwondo athletes at the Paralympic Games was concentrated in the late twenties, with female athletes showing a younger age profile than males, suggesting a consistent age pattern in this Paralympic combat sport.

title: Pathways to the podium: age and technical-tactical factors associated with medalling in Para Judo
title_original: Pathways to the podium: age and technical-tactical factors associated with medalling in Para Judo
summary: This study aimed to explore factors associated with medalling in Para judo at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games, focusing on athlete characteristics and technical-tactical variables. Using published competition results, medalling outcomes for men and women were separately modelled using Bayesian penalised regression. Models included age, body weight, sport class, throws, groundwork techniques, and penalties per match. Results are reported as posterior probabilities that the regression coefficient was greater or less than zero, Pr(β > 0) or Pr(β < 0), according to the direction of the posterior mean. In males, age showed a predominantly negative posterior distribution (Pr[β < 0] = .944), whereas body weight (Pr[β > 0] = .972), throws (Pr[β > 0] >.999), groundwork techniques (Pr[β > 0] >.999), and penalties (Pr[β > 0] = .962) showed predominantly positive posterior distributions. In females, throws and groundwork techniques showed positive associations with medalling (both Pr[β > 0] >.999), whereas age (Pr[β < 0] = .818) and penalties (Pr[β < 0] = .801) showed predominantly negative posterior distributions with greater uncertainty. Overall, throws and groundwork techniques showed the most consistent positive associations with medalling across both sex-specific models. These findings may inform technical-tactical priorities and long-term athlete development in Para judo.

title: Adaptive Sports and Social Reintegration
title_original: Adaptive Sports and Social Reintegration
summary: Purpose: This study aimed to examine the role of participation in adaptive sports in the process of social reintegration among individuals with acquired physical disabilities, with a specific focus on para alpine skiing. Particular attention was given to the development of athletic identity and life satisfaction. Methods: This qualitative study formed part of a broader sequential mixed-method investigation. Following a quantitative phase involving 129 para alpine skiers, semi-structured interviews were conducted with six purposively selected elite para alpine skiers who participated in the Sochi 2014 Winter Paralympic Games to complement and deepen the quantitative findings. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis informed by grounded theory principles, allowing for the identification of key categories and relationships within the resocialisation process. Results: The findings indicate that participation in adaptive sports, particularly para alpine skiing, plays a central role in social reintegration after disability. Athletes reported significant improvements in life satisfaction, driven by increased independence, structured daily routines, and meaningful goal-oriented activity. The reconstruction of athletic identity emerged as a key mechanism underlying psychological adaptation, contributing to enhanced self-concept and self-efficacy. In addition, participation in adaptive sports facilitated the expansion of social networks and strengthened interpersonal relationships, supporting broader social reintegration. However, the process was influenced by contextual factors, such as financial constraints and access to sports infrastructure. Conclusions: Adaptive sports participation represents a critical pathway for social reintegration, promoting life satisfaction and athletic identity development among individuals with disabilities. These findings highlight the importance of reducing structural barriers and ensuring equitable access to sport as part of comprehensive rehabilitation strategies.

title: Prevalence and patterns of sports supplement use in elite wheelchair basketball players: an analysis based on the AIS framework
title_original: Prevalence and patterns of sports supplement use in elite wheelchair basketball players: an analysis based on the AIS framework
summary: Background Sports supplement use is widespread in elite sport, yet evidence regarding supplementation practices in Paralympic team sports remains limited. Wheelchair basketball players present specific physiological and contextual characteristics that may influence supplement use and its alignment with current scientific evidence. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted in 66 elite Spanish wheelchair basketball players (57 men and 9 women) from 10 first-division teams. Participants completed a validated questionnaire assessing self-reported sports supplement use, reasons for consumption, and sources of information. Supplements were classified according to the Australian Institute of Sport (AIS) framework based on scientific evidence and safety. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed to examine associations between self-reported sports supplement use and athlete characteristics, including sex, functional classification, and training profile. Results Overall, 72.7% of athletes reported current self-reported sports supplement use. Expressed as proportions of the entire sample ( n = 66), Group A products were consumed by 66.7% of athletes, Group B products by 31.8%, while no athletes reported using Group C (0%) or Group D (0%) substances. Protein supplements, creatine monohydrate, and caffeine were the most frequently consumed products. Supplement use patterns were generally similar across sex and functional classifications, although no statistically significant differences were observed. title: Epidemiological profile of musculoskeletal injuries in professional kata athletes: a retrospective descriptive study
title_original: Epidemiological profile of musculoskeletal injuries in professional kata athletes: a retrospective descriptive study
summary: Exposure-adjusted injury risk in high-intensity kata performance remains poorly characterized. This study quantified the incidence, distribution, and context of musculoskeletal injuries among professional kata athletes. In a retrospective descriptive study, 210 Iranian Super League athletes (104 males, 106 females; mean ± SD age 23.5 ± 4.7 years) completed a standardized interview and an injury record form adapted from the International Olympic Committee surveillance system. Exposure was expressed as athlete-minutes across an 86-day pre-competition phase and a 3-day competition phase. Injury incidence (events/1000 athlete-minutes) with 95% CIs was estimated via Poisson methods; incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were calculated using Poisson regression with an exposure offset. Pearson’s chi-square tests were used to investigate the relationship between sex and categorical injury variables, including injury type, nature, and anatomical area. Of the 210 athletes, 112 (53.3%) sustained 138 injuries during 7,380 athlete-minutes of exposure (training: 6795; competition: 585). The overall injury incidence was 18.7 per 1,000 athlete-minutes (95% CI: 15.71–22.05). title: Predictive Governance: The Management Dilemmas of AI-Driven Anti-Doping Education
title_original: Predictive Governance: The Management Dilemmas of AI-Driven Anti-Doping Education
summary: The integration of artificial intelligence into anti-doping governance represents a paradigmatic shift from reactive enforcement to predictive regulation, yet the educational dimensions of this transformation remain critically under-theorized. This article addresses the immediate 2026 technological disruption in sports administration by developing a conceptual framework for understanding the management dilemmas inherent in AI-driven anti-doping education. Drawing on a policy analysis of institutional documents, regulatory frameworks, and emerging technological applications across European, North American, and Asian contexts, the study identifies three fundamental tensions: the paradox of personalization versus standardization in educational content delivery; the conflict between algorithmic efficiency and athlete autonomy in risk assessment; and the governance gap between technological capability and regulatory accountability. The analysis reveals that AI-enhanced anti-doping education operates within a predictive governance logic that prioritizes pre-emptive intervention over deliberative engagement, generating what we term "algorithmic compliance" rather than ethical internalization. The article proposes a reflexive governance framework that integrates technical innovation with participatory oversight, athlete-centred design principles, and regulatory coherence. Recommendations address the imperative for WADA and national anti-doping organizations to develop binding standards for AI transparency, athlete data rights, and human oversight mechanisms in educational interventions. The findings contribute to broader debates on the governance of algorithmic systems in sport and the preservation of athlete agency within increasingly datafied regulatory environments. The analysis proceeded through a three-phase analytical procedure—descriptive mapping, hybrid inductive–deductive thematic coding, and framework construction—applied to the 28 institutional and regulatory documents, the technological cases, and the regulatory frameworks described below.

title: Illuminating Olympicenes: Insights Into Anti‐Kasha Photophysics in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
title_original: Illuminating Olympicenes: Insights Into Anti‐Kasha Photophysics in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
summary: ABSTRACT Olympicene, or 6 H ‐benzo[ cd ]pyrene, is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) with five fused six‐membered rings arranged in a pattern reminiscent of the Olympic symbol. While functionalized olympicene‐based materials have captivated attention for their unique graphene‐fragment topology and aromaticity, their photoluminescent properties remain virtually unexplored. Here, we synthesize olympicene‐core functionalized derivatives and report their “anomalous” photophysical properties. These olympicene derivatives display extensive vibronic structure and highly interacting electronic states. Such effects give rise to excited‐state dynamics that are rare and unconventional in small PAH systems. Specifically, these olympicene derivatives exhibit dual fluorescence upon photoexcitation, accompanied by pronounced excitation‐dependent emission behavior. Spectroscopic evidence demonstrates these behaviors arise from multiple singlet emissive states—an anti‐Kasha locally excited (LE) state ( S n , n ≥ 2) and an intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) state. This work positions olympicene‐functionalized derivatives as a new platform to study fundamental photophysics. Exploring these properties will lead to new and advanced optoelectronic applications.
