title: Uma investigação da matriz ética e moral desportiva
title_original: Uma investigação da matriz ética e moral desportiva
summary: This work, which is philosophical in nature and focuses on the field of sports, aims to conduct transdisciplinary research on ethical principles and the formation of the moral foundation of sports. Thus, through a literature review on the subject, it discusses historical concepts and studies of morality and the human ethical framework as the foundation and driving force of the evolutionary process. Thus, it highlights the schools of thought that have influenced modern sporting ideology and normative and educational practices, such as the Olympic tradition of fair play and its benefits for moral education. As a result of the study, concepts were identified that support the initial hypothesis and provide a scientific basis for research into the roots of sports ethics and morality.

title: Transforming India’s Sports Ecosystem for Global Sporting Excellence
title_original: Transforming India’s Sports Ecosystem for Global Sporting Excellence
summary: In today’s world, sports are no longer just an entertainment medium or physical activity but have become a powerful tool for Health, Educational Development, Employment Generation, and Social Inclusion, National Pride, Economic Progress, and Youth Empowerment. It has thus been necessary for India, being a large and young country, to create a sound, inclusive, and sustainable sports ecosystem. A sports ecosystem refers to a linked system in which various factors such as sports infrastructure, talent detection, coaching, sports science, medicine, education, competitions, finance, and employment come together to form a whole. Though there is no dearth of sports talent in India, what is missing is an effective system for talent identification, cultivation, and elevation to the international level. Khelo India, Fit India, and the Olympic Podium Scheme are some of the steps taken in this direction. Khelo Bharat Niti-2025, launched in this year, stresses the need for connecting sports to national building, economic growth, social development, and mass movement. This article discusses the importance of creating a strong sports ecosystem in India, its current situation, the main challenges it is facing, the opportunities and ways for developing it. It concludes that a holistic sports system from grassroots sports to elite sports is necessary for India, instead of focusing only on winning medals.

title: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
title_original: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
summary: Efficient, ultrapure green organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) fabricated via wet processing are crucial for ultrahigh definition displays but remain highly challenging due to the paucity of suitable emitters. Herein, we developed Oly-BN, a novel multipleresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitter featuring a distinct Olympic-patterned boron-distribution. The zigzag doped heteroatom polycyclic aromatic framework enables near-degenerate singlet/triplet excited states. Integrating para-N-π-B motifs helps regulate the triplet manifold and emission color point, enabling energetically accessible higher lying triplet excited states with enhanced spinorbit coupling, while also suppressing low-frequency structural relaxation and modulating the optical bandgap. Oly-BN in toluene exhibits vivid green emission at 522 nm with a narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 17 nm, a photoluminescence quantum yield of 95%, and a fast reverse intersystem crossing rate constant of 6.9×106 s−1. Additionally, its highly twisted conformation weakens intermolecular interactions and favors bright, solid-state emission. The nonsensitized solution-processed OLEDs deliver ultrapure green electroluminescence with a CIEy value up to 0.73, and achieves an optimized maximum external quantum efficiency of 39.4%, which remains high at 29.9% at 1000 cd m-2. This work not only provides a promising highly saturated green emitter for solution-processed OLEDs but also demonstrates the importance of precisely integrating heteroatoms in modulating photophysical properties of MR-TADF emitters.

title: From norms to practice: benchmarking International Sports Federations against the UN anti-corruption framework
title_original: From norms to practice: benchmarking International Sports Federations against the UN anti-corruption framework
summary: Abstract International Sports Federations (ISFs) occupy a structurally unique position in the global governance landscape: private associations incorporated under Swiss civil law that simultaneously exercise binding transnational regulatory authority over their respective sports domains. While Swiss association law is the dominant legal form across the Olympic Movement, this sample is intentionally jurisdictionally diverse, spanning Swiss, German, British, and Malaysian entities. Since each of these jurisdictions is party to UNCAC, the UNODC benchmark applies consistently across the sample irrespective of where each federation is headquarted. Although the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (United Nations 2004) and a comprehensive suite of UNODC guidance instruments have established precise standards for private organisations, no systematic empirical study has evaluated the extent to which ISF anti-corruption frameworks reflect these standards. This study addresses that gap through a researcher-led normative document benchmarking study of six summer Olympic ISFs, selected across three governance tiers identified by the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations (ASOIF) governance assessment. Employing a 41-question, four-point scoring instrument derived directly from five UNODC source documents, the study evaluates each ISF’s publicly available governance instruments against eight dimensions: leadership commitment, risk assessment, prohibited conduct scope, financial integrity, conflict of interest management, reporting mechanisms, training and education, and enforcement architecture. The findings reveal a structural pattern of partial alignment: ISFs demonstrate reasonable policy coverage at the level of normative commitments but systematic deficiency at the operational and oversight levels. Most critically, all six federations exhibit a significant deficit of internal financial crime controls. This absence encompasses gaps in corruption risk assessment, post-employment restrictions, and the structural independence of investigatory functions. The study concludes with a typology of governance archetypes observable across the cohort and targeted policy recommendations grounded in the UNODC normative architecture.

summary_ru: Abstract International Sports Federations (ISFs) occupy a structurally unique position in the global governance landscape: private associations incorporated under Swiss civil law that simultaneously exercise binding transnational regulatory authority over their respective sports domains. While Swiss association law is the dominant legal form across the Olympic Movement, this sample is intentionally jurisdictionally diverse, spanning Swiss, German, British, and Malaysian entities. Since each of these jurisdictions is party to UNCAC, the UNODC benchmark applies consistently across the sample irrespective of where each federation is headquarted. Although the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (United Nations 2004) and a comprehensive suite of UNODC guidance instruments have established precise standards for private organisations, no systematic empirical study has evaluated the extent to which ISF anti-corruption frameworks reflect these standards. This study addresses that gap through a researcher-led normative document benchmarking study of six summer Olympic ISFs, selected across three governance tiers identified by the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations (ASOIF) governance assessment. Employing a 41-question, four-point scoring instrument derived directly from five UNODC source documents, the study evaluates each ISF’s publicly available governance instruments against eight dimensions: leadership commitment, risk assessment, prohibited conduct scope, financial integrity, conflict of interest management, reporting mechanisms, training and education, and enforcement architecture. The findings reveal a structural pattern of partial alignment: ISFs demonstrate reasonable policy coverage at the level of normative commitments but systematic deficiency at the operational and oversight levels. Most critically, all six federations exhibit a significant deficit of internal financial crime controls. This absence encompasses gaps in corruption risk assessment, post-employment restrictions, and the structural independence of investigatory functions. The study concludes with a typology of governance archetypes observable across the cohort and targeted policy recommendations grounded in the UNODC normative architecture.

title: Homo Olympicus: Olimpismo como instrumento de formação humana
title_original: Homo Olympicus: Olimpismo como instrumento de formação humana
summary: In Brazil, Physical Education training has historically favored biological and technicist approaches to the detriment of philosophical, sociological and humanistic foundations aimed at the integral understanding of the human being. In this context, Olympism, conceived by Pierre de Coubertin as a philosophy of life based on the balance between body, mind and spirit, presents itself as an important pedagogical possibility for contemporary physical education. This theoretical essay aimed to analyze the concept of Homo Olympicus in contemporary society and discuss how Olympic Education can contribute to human formation in the context of contemporary educational and school sport. It is a theoretical essay, with a qualitative approach and analytical-descriptive character, based on bibliographic review and documentary analysis. The theoretical path was structured from the category’s philosophy of education, sports pedagogy, corporeality, fair play, educational sport and the anthropological concepts of Homo Ludens, Homo Gymnasticus, Homo Sportivus and Homo Olympicus. The results indicate that Olympic Education expands the pedagogical possibilities of sport by overcoming the restricted logic of performance and hypercompetitiveness, valuing principles such as respect, friendship, cooperation, excellence and citizenship. It was also evidenced that informal fair play and the valorization of corporeality contribute to overcoming reductionist perspectives present in school Physical Education. It is concluded that Olympism can be understood as a philosophy of education and a formative instrument for the construction of critical, autonomous and socially committed subjects.

title: Tirzepatide in Sport after Inclusion in the WADA Monitoring Program: An Updated Narrative Review of Body Composition, Muscle Preservation and Potential Performance Implications
title_original: Tirzepatide in Sport after Inclusion in the WADA Monitoring Program: An Updated Narrative Review of Body Composition, Muscle Preservation and Potential Performance Implications
summary: Background: Tirzepatide, as a dual agonist of the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors, has become one of the most effective pharmacological therapies used to treat obesity and metabolic disorders. Growing interest in its potential use among physically active individuals and the inclusion of tirzepatide markers in the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) monitoring program for 2026 highlight the need to reassess the significance of this substance in sports. Aim: The aim of this study was to update the available data on tirzepatide in the context of sports. Material and methods: A narrative review of the current literature on tirzepatide, incretin receptor agonists and their use in the context of sports was conducted. The analysis included clinical trials, systematic reviews, publications on body composition, metabolism, and exercise adaptation, as well as WADA regulatory documents. Results: Tirzepatide effectively reduces body weight and improves metabolic parameters. However, available evidence mainly concerns individuals with obesity or type 2 diabetes, rather than athletes. Changes in lean body mass during therapy may be relevant for physically active individuals, especially in sports requiring high strength and power. Although weight reduction could be beneficial in weight-class sports. Further studies are needed to assess the long-term impact of tirzepatide on athletic performance and to address the ethical issues associated with its use. Conclusions: Tirzepatide currently has no proven effect on enhancing athletic performance. However, its impact on body weight and body composition may be important for athletes. The inclusion of tirzepatide in WADA’s monitoring program highlights the need for further research into its potential misuse, its effects on muscle, and the long-term consequences of its utilization in the athletic population.

title: Identidad de género y deporte: debate en X sobre la participación de Imane Khelif en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024
title_original: Identidad de género y deporte: debate en X sobre la participación de Imane Khelif en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024
summary: Purpose: This study analyses the polarisation of public discourse on the social network X (formerly Twitter) surrounding Algerian boxer Imane Khelif's participation in the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. The aim is to examine how different positions on gender identity, fairness and legitimacy in elite sport are constructed, disseminated and contested. Methodology: A total of 35,676 posts from 25,984 unique users were collected and analysed using the professional tool Tweet Binder during the period 27 July to 10 August 2024. Automated sentiment analysis based on natural language processing (NLP) was applied, classifying posts into four categories (positive, negative, neutral and undefined), supplemented by temporal, linguistic and key-actor analysis. Results: Significant polarisation was identified. Although positive posts outnumbered negative ones (18% versus 17%), critical publications generated twice as many impressions (194.8 million versus 93.3 million). Public figures such as Elon Musk and J.K. Rowling amplified the controversy with posts exceeding 670 million combined views. Activity peaks coincided with key events such as Angela Carini's withdrawal. Conclusions: Social media platforms function as spaces of symbolic confrontation where emotionally negative content achieves greater reach. Misinformation about the athlete's medical condition fuelled reductionist narratives. Digital discourse may influence future sports regulations on inclusion and fairness.

title: The Landscape of Doping in Indian Sports: Contemporary Challenges and Deliberations
title_original: The Landscape of Doping in Indian Sports: Contemporary Challenges and Deliberations
summary: The menace of doping in the Indian sporting ecosystem is well acknowledged, but the social ramifications of the process have not been explored in depth. The paper aims to reflect upon the intricate social dynamics of doping structured by various socio-economic factors, cultural narratives, and the widespread availability of doping substances. Through ethnographic fieldwork in western Uttar Pradesh (India), the study uncovers the practice of doping among junior athletes, a significant lack of awareness of anti-doping frameworks among junior/adolescent athletes and Athlete Support Personnel (ASP) regarding anti-doping policies. It highlights the crucial role of suppliers in fostering a dopogenic environment. The findings illustrate a concerning landscape where regulatory efforts and initiatives by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) in India encounter obstacles due to a deficiency in the reach of educational frameworks and a cultural perception of doping as a pathway to success. The paper advocates for an intersectional approach to anti-doping frameworks, stressing the importance of collaboration among stakeholders to cultivate a culture of fair play, particularly in India&s;s aspirations to host the 2036 Olympic Games.

Through ethnographic fieldwork in western Uttar Pradesh (India), the study uncovers the practice of doping among junior athletes, a significant lack of awareness of anti-doping frameworks among junior/adolescent athletes and Athlete Support Personnel (ASP) regarding anti-doping policies. It highlights the crucial role of suppliers in fostering a dopogenic environment. The findings illustrate a concerning landscape where regulatory efforts and initiatives by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) in India encounter obstacles due to a deficiency in the reach of educational frameworks and a cultural perception of doping as a pathway to success. The paper advocates for an intersectional approach to anti-doping frameworks, stressing the importance of collaboration among stakeholders to cultivate a culture of fair play, particularly in India&s;s aspirations to host the 2036 Olympic Games.

title: Historiographical dimensions of Ukrainian physical culture and sport: a bibliometric analysis of the global scholarly discourse (1991–2025)
title_original: Historiographical dimensions of Ukrainian physical culture and sport: a bibliometric analysis of the global scholarly discourse (1991–2025)
summary: The article analyses the scholarly discourse on the history of the system of physical education, sport and physical activity in Ukraine in contemporary periodicals. Background and aim of the study. The globalisation of science makes it necessary to examine how the Ukrainian past is reflected in international scholarly works, which is essential for overcoming the sense of inferiority and for decolonising national history. Despite the existence of individual reviews, a comprehensive analysis of international publications is still lacking, and researchers have not yet clarified the specific features of how the history of Ukrainian sport and physical culture is being integrated into the global academic space. The aim of the study is to substantiate, on the basis of an analysis of an international body of publications (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, 1991–2025), the distinctive nature of the Ukrainian history of physical culture and sport as a sociocultural phenomenon and to identify the main thematic areas of its current research. Material and methods. Using bibliometric and comparative analysis methods, a representative body of publications (1991–2025) was examined. The structural and systemic approach made it possible to classify and organise this body of documents according to key thematic clusters. Results. The quantitative analysis revealed a growth in the number of publications (up to 7.6 works per year in 2016–2025), with periodicals (89%) and foreign authors (64%) predominating. Qualitative content analysis made it possible to identify five key thematic areas: physical culture and sport as an ideological and political instrument (using the example of the Soviet system and current sports sanctions); the role of national forms of physical activity and body practices (Sokil, Plast, Fighting Hopak) in shaping identity; the development of sport in the context of modernisation processes and urban history; the evolution of health-enhancing and recreational physical culture, from the therapeutic gymnastics of the early 20th century to the modern fitness industry; and the grassroots self-organisation of physical culture and sports societies. Conclusions. The analysis showed an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented renewal of Ukrainian historiography of physical culture and sport. Overcoming the identified chronological and regional imbalances through methodological modernisation is a promising direction for future global research.

title: The Biomechanical and Perceptual Impact of Breast Support during Riding and Running in Female Equestrians
title_original: The Biomechanical and Perceptual Impact of Breast Support during Riding and Running in Female Equestrians
summary: Popular among women, equestrian sport is the only sex-integrated Olympic sport, relying on interspecies communication between horse and rider. Despite extensive breast research in sport, equestrian research is limited. This study investigated the impact of bras on breast movement, comfort, and pain; rider position and asymmetry; and compared breast movement and pain in riding versus running. Participants (n = 21) rode a Racewood™ Equine Simulator (ES) in walk, trot, and canter and ran on a treadmill (TM) in four breast support conditions: everyday (EB), encapsulation sports bra (ESB), combination sports bra (CSB), and bare-breasted (BB). Markers were tracked by a Qualisys motion capture system, and relative breast displacement (RBD) in TM and ES was calculated, along with rider position during ES. Exercise-induced breast pain (EIBP) and bra comfort were measured on 0–100 visual analogue scales, and a survey on bra performance and aesthetics was completed. title: Sportswashing and the Paradoxes of CSR: A critical public relations model of elite sports philanthropy
title_original: Sportswashing and the Paradoxes of CSR: A critical public relations model of elite sports philanthropy
summary: This article revisits a foundational question in critical public relations (CPR): how do we distinguish corporate social responsibility (CSR) grounded in genuine public interests from CSR activities that are strategically mobilized for reputational advantage? It addresses this question by exploring sportswashing, conceptualized here as a reputational outcome of sports philanthropy, particularly the sponsorship of elite athletes. It analyzes this phenomenon through a case study of Australian mining magnate Gina Rinehart and her sponsorships of elite Olympic athletes. It identifies the earned media publicity generated from these sponsorships through qualitative content analysis of Australian newspapers. The findings show that this coverage overwhelmingly framed Rinehart as a benevolent benefactor of Olympic sport, associating her with charismatic athletes and more abstract constructs such as patriotism and national glory. Ultimately, the article develops a critical public relations model of sportswashing (CPRMS) intended as a theoretical disruption of uncritical accounts of CSR. This model demonstrates that sports philanthropy, while clearly beneficial to athletes, can also serve as a tool for image bolstering in the service of private capital.

title: Athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and audience engagement in CCTV News’s Olympic short-video coverage on Douyin: an empirical analysis
title_original: Athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and audience engagement in CCTV News’s Olympic short-video coverage on Douyin: an empirical analysis
summary: Short-form video platforms have become important channels for major sports-event coverage, but empirical evidence remains limited regarding how athletes are presented, how emotions are organized, and how these features relate to audience engagement in specific institutional accounts. This study analyzes 219 short-video posts published by the official China Central Television (CCTV) News account on Douyin during the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. Content analysis, t-tests, and regression analysis were used to examine mention-based athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and three platform-displayed engagement indicators: likes, comments, and shares. The results show no statistically significant difference between female and male athletes in mention frequency, indicating relative balance only at the level of being named. Athlete mention frequency was not significantly associated with likes, comments, or shares. Emotional narratives were not directly associated with higher engagement, but posts using emotional narratives contained significantly more athlete mentions. Emotional narrative also positively moderated the relationship between mention frequency and shares, although not the relationships with likes or comments. These findings suggest that, within this single-account and single-platform case, mention frequency is a potential narrative resource rather than an engagement outcome in itself, and its association with content diffusion depends partly on emotional framing. The conclusions should not be generalized to all Chinese mainstream media or interpreted as evidence of complete gender equality in athlete portrayal.

title: A fada do skate e o empoderamento do mito: A perspectiva feminista na construção publicitária de Rayssa Leal durante as Olimpíadas de Tóquio 2020
title_original: A fada do skate e o empoderamento do mito: A perspectiva feminista na construção publicitária de Rayssa Leal durante as Olimpíadas de Tóquio 2020
summary: Rayssa Leal was only six years old when she was nicknamed "Fadinha" (Little Fairy), a moniker that bridged the playful world of children's stories with skateboarding and contributed to building her mythic image in the media landscape. Against this backdrop, this study analyzes the representation of the Brazilian athlete in advertising media related to the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games, viewed through the lens of female empowerment. To this end, the study employs the film analysis framework proposed by Vanoye and Goliot-Lété (2006), applying it to keyframes from the "Novas Fadas" (New Fairies) commercial produced by Nike. The theoretical framework integrates concepts of myth, advertising, and gender equity, while also addressing "Femvertising" and its implications for contemporary representations of women. The results indicate that the campaign constructs a mythic, inspirational image of Rayssa Leal through visual elements, animation, and soundtrack, reinforcing values ​​associated with overcoming obstacles and realizing dreams. Concurrently, the narrative mobilizes discourses regarding gender equality and the valuing of women's presence in historically male-dominated spaces, positioning the athlete as a symbolic figure of inspiration, representation, and social transformation.

title: Casting On at the Games: Knitting Through Milano Cortina
title_original: Casting On at the Games: Knitting Through Milano Cortina
summary: This study examined how Olympic athletes shared knitting-themed content on Instagram before, during, and after the Milano Cortina Winter Games in early 2026, with particular attention paid to the themes associated with posts. Instagram has been recognized as a key platform for craft-related content among makers, and it has also served as a central space for athletes’ personal brand building. The research data were collected from athletes’ public Instagram accounts, including images and Reels, up to April 10, 2026, at which point several recurring narratives and themes reached a natural conclusion as the season ended. The findings suggest that athletes utilized social media to curate their personal brands. They framed knitting as a relaxing and enjoyable activity to balance intensive training schedules and traveling. Many emphasized the importance of finalizing knitting projects and described a sense of satisfaction and pleasure upon finishing them. A notable practice involved the “Knitting Club,” where athletes gathered face-to-face during the Olympic Games. Interaction between athletes and their followers was frequent, with numerous comments in the comment sections and shared challenges. Overall, the dialogue was predominantly positive and supportive, highlighting knitting as a means of expressing identity and building community in elite sports contexts.

title: Dynamics of the Competitiveness of Russian Male and Female Pole Vaulters During the 2020–2024 Olympic Cycle
title_original: Dynamics of the Competitiveness of Russian Male and Female Pole Vaulters During the 2020–2024 Olympic Cycle
summary: The level of competitiveness in pole vaulting reflects not only athletic performance but also the effectiveness of athlete development within the discipline. This study examines changes in the competitive dynamics of Russian male and female pole vaulters during the 2020–2024 Olympic cycle and identifies factors associated with these changes. The analysis was based on official results from the Russian Indoor and Outdoor Athletics Championships. Competitive dynamics were assessed using a combination of literature review, comparative analysis of competition results, calculation of competitiveness coefficients, statistical analysis, and expert consultations with experienced pole vault specialists. The results indicate a gradual decline in competitiveness in the women’s event, accompanied by lower performance density and a widening gap between leading athletes and the remainder of the field. In contrast, the men’s event demonstrated relatively stable competitive characteristics throughout the study period. These findings provide an empirical assessment of the current state of the discipline and may contribute to improving long-term athlete development, optimizing competition planning, and monitoring the effectiveness of pole vault development programmes.

title: From “Growth” to “Healing”
title_original: From “Growth” to “Healing”
summary: In 2026, Mango TV aired the fifth season of Dad in Charge under the theme “Dad in Charge: Give Yourself a Hug.” While continuing the narrative of men’s growth through childrearing, the season shifts the focus of emotional communication from validating fathers’ parenting competence toward accepting parental exhaustion and imperfection, marking a turn from a growth narrative to a healing narrative. Taking the documentary footage, observation-studio segments, and danmu comments concerning the season’s four families as its objects of analysis, this study examines the narrative configuration and communication mechanisms underlying this shift. It finds that, through differentiated family samples—dual-income households, a large extended family, and a cross-cultural sojourning family—the program offers viewers four affective positions: guilt, uplift, clumsiness, and ease. Through affective triggering in the documentary footage, mirroring guidance in the observation studio, and social diffusion via danmu comments, the program completes a communication chain that runs from individual emotion to public discussion. The healing turn responds to the emotional needs of childbearing-age families in a low-fertility context and performs a function of sociocultural mediation; media consolation, however, cannot substitute for resolving structural difficulties in childrearing, and the healing narrative also risks the superficialization of emotion.

title: The Ubiquitous Role of the Smartphone in Breaking: An Ethnographic-Informed Study
title_original: The Ubiquitous Role of the Smartphone in Breaking: An Ethnographic-Informed Study
summary: Breaking is a physically demanding street dance, which is highly creative and historically rooted in urban culture. Studies about Breaking are scant, and the role of technology in the modality, e.g., smartphones, while potentially relevant according to a previous technology review, is still unknown. This study is a first step into understanding the role of technology in Breaking. Drawing on observations of 35 training sessions and 15 interviews with Non-Professional to Olympic-level Breakers, we found that smartphones act as digital scaffolds for Breaking. Smartphone use supports training structure, movement arsenal management, performance improvement and creativity, and peer feedback and community engagement. Our contribution is two-fold: we first contribute a detailed understanding of how smartphones mediate Breaking, a form of appropriating the smartphone which has not been previously described; then, we outline design opportunities for future systems aimed at Breaking and other modalities, which are non-hierarchical, heavily rooted in culture, and turn to peer-to-peer expertise exchange to develop complex physical practices.

title: Women's participation in the Paralympic Games (1960–2024): a longitudinal and bibliometric analysis of global trends and scientific production
title_original: Women's participation in the Paralympic Games (1960–2024): a longitudinal and bibliometric analysis of global trends and scientific production
summary: Background Women's participation in the Paralympic Games has expanded over time, yet this growth has been non-linear and uneven across regions, disciplines, and editions. At the same time, scientific research on women in Paralympic and parasports contexts remains limited and geographically concentrated. Studies that provide a comprehensive, long-term, sex-disaggregated reconstruction of participation across both Summer and Winter editions, together with an examination of its relationship to the geography of scientific production, are scarce. Methods This study reconstructs sex-disaggregated participation in the Summer Paralympic Games (1960–2024) and Winter Paralympic Games (1976–2022) using official data provided by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC), harmonized with National Paralympic Committee data. Longitudinal trends and cross-national patterns are examined through descriptive and comparative analyses. Exploratory non-parametric analyses were used to assess longitudinal trends and macro-regional differences in demographic-normalized participation. As a complementary component, a systematic search of the Web of Science Core Collection (completed 31 October 2025) identified 71 relevant publications, which were analyzed using bibliometric techniques. Results Women's participation in the Summer Paralympics follows a non-linear trajectory, reaching near parity at Paris 2024 (44.4%), whereas participation in the Winter Games remains consistently lower, with only modest long-term growth and no comparable movement toward parity (18%–25%). Two study-specific descriptive indicators, i.e., the Weighted Equity Index and the Normalized Female Participation Index, were used to summarize cross-national differences in internal delegation balance and demographic-normalized participation intensity. The bibliometric analysis documents a small but expanding body of literature that is geographically concentrated. Conclusion These findings suggest a persistent misalignment between the increasing presence of women in the Paralympic Games and the comparatively limited and uneven development of scientific research on this population. The study provides a comprehensive longitudinal mapping of women's participation and offers an empirical basis for future research and policy aimed at improving equity in Paralympic sports.

title: The ımpact of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ ımagery skills
title_original: The ımpact of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ ımagery skills
summary: Background and Study Aim. Imagery has increasingly gained attention as a mental training technique in the field of sport psychology. Many Olympic and elite athletes effectively employ imagery training to enhance their performance. Although a substantial body of research has demonstrated the positive effects of imagery training on athletic performance, further research is still needed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of these interventions. In this context, the present study aims to examine the effects of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ imagery abilities. Method: A total of 30 athletes participated in this study; 15 were assigned to the experimental group and 15 to the control group. The participants were selected from university team athletes competing in basketball, football, and volleyball. The study was conducted using a quasi-experimental design within the framework of quantitative research methods. Data were collected using the Movement Imagery Questionnaire, the d2 Test of Attention, and the n-back test. A repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to examine time-dependent changes between the experimental and control groups. Results: The findings indicate that the six-week visual attention and visual memory training program did not have a significant effect on athletes’ visual attention skills; however, it led to improvements in their visual memory abilities. Furthermore, analyses conducted in the second phase of the study revealed that, in line with improvements in visual memory, athletes also demonstrated enhanced imagery abilities. Conclusion: The results suggest that the implemented visual memory exercises significantly improved athletes’ visual memory performance, and that this improvement was associated with notable enhancements in both kinesthetic and visual imagery abilities. In contrast, the visual attention exercises did not produce a statistically significant effect on attention performance. Overall, visual memory appears to play a central role in the cognitive foundations of imagery ability.

Furthermore, analyses conducted in the second phase of the study revealed that, in line with improvements in visual memory, athletes also demonstrated enhanced imagery abilities. Conclusion: The results suggest that the implemented visual memory exercises significantly improved athletes’ visual memory performance, and that this improvement was associated with notable enhancements in both kinesthetic and visual imagery abilities. In contrast, the visual attention exercises did not produce a statistically significant effect on attention performance. Overall, visual memory appears to play a central role in the cognitive foundations of imagery ability.
summary_original: Background and Study Aim. Imagery has increasingly gained attention as a mental training technique in the field of sport psychology. Many Olympic and elite athletes effectively employ imagery training to enhance their performance. Although a substantial body of research has demonstrated the positive effects of imagery training on athletic performance, further research is still needed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of these interventions. In this context, the present study aims to examine the effects of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ imagery abilities. Method: A total of 30 athletes participated in this study; 15 were assigned to the experimental group and 15 to the control group. The participants were selected from university team athletes competing in basketball, football, and volleyball. The study was conducted using a quasi-experimental design within the framework of quantitative research methods. Data were collected using the Movement Imagery Questionnaire, the d2 Test of Attention, and the n-back test. A repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to examine time-dependent changes between the experimental and control groups. Results: The findings indicate that the six-week visual attention and visual memory training program did not have a significant effect on athletes’ visual attention skills; however, it led to improvements in their visual memory abilities. Furthermore, analyses conducted in the second phase of the study revealed that, in line with improvements in visual memory, athletes also demonstrated enhanced imagery abilities. Conclusion: The results suggest that the implemented visual memory exercises significantly improved athletes’ visual memory performance, and that this improvement was associated with notable enhancements in both kinesthetic and visual imagery abilities. In contrast, the visual attention exercises did not produce a statistically significant effect on attention performance. Overall, visual memory appears to play a central role in the cognitive foundations of imagery ability.

title: ВЛИЯНИЕ ПРОВЕДЕНИЯ ИГР ОЛИМПИАД НА МЕДАЛЬНЫЕ ПОКАЗАТЕЛИ СТРАНЫ-ОРГАНИЗАТОРА
title_original: ВЛИЯНИЕ ПРОВЕДЕНИЯ ИГР ОЛИМПИАД НА МЕДАЛЬНЫЕ ПОКАЗАТЕЛИ СТРАНЫ-ОРГАНИЗАТОРА
summary: Проведен анализ влияния фактора домашних Игр Олимпиады на медальные показатели национальных олимпийских сборных команд стран-организаторов. Установлено, что в среднем страны-организаторы завоевывают на домашних Играх медалей больше, чем на двух предыдущих. Выявлены страны с наибольшим приростом медальных показателей: Мексика (1968), Великобритания (1908), США (1904). Определены страны, сохранившие спортивное олимпийское наследие на последующих Играх лучше всего: Канада, Швеция, Испания, Великобритания, Южная Корея. Установлено, что в среднем медальные показатели на двух последующих Играх превышают показатели двух предыдущих. Выявлены страны, снизившие медальные показатели после домашних Игр: Германия, США после 1996 и 1932 гг., Италия, Бельгия, Финляндия, Греция.

title: AN INTEGRATED MULTI-INSTRUMENT FRAMEWORK FOR OPERATIONAL AVALANCHE RISK MANAGEMENT: THE MILANO CORTINA 2026 WINTER OLYMPICS IN LIVIGNO, ITALY
title_original: AN INTEGRATED MULTI-INSTRUMENT FRAMEWORK FOR OPERATIONAL AVALANCHE RISK MANAGEMENT: THE MILANO CORTINA 2026 WINTER OLYMPICS IN LIVIGNO, ITALY
summary: Avalanche risk management in complex alpine environments increasingly relies on the integration of heterogeneous data sources and modelling approaches into a coherent operational framework.During the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games, an advanced multi-layer system was implemented in Livigno (Italy) to support real-time decision-making for avalanche risk mitigation affecting critical infrastructures.The system combined in situ measurements and field observations, automatic detection technologies, numerical weather model (NWM) data, snowpack modelling and avalanche dynamics simulations within a unified operational environment.Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) provided continuous observations of key meteorological and snow variables, forming the basis for both process interpretation and model forcing.These data were complemented by NWM outputs, used both as forecast products and as input for snowpack simulations.Snowpack evolution was simulated using the SNOWPACK model, providing stratigraphic information, stability indices and forecasts of typical avalanche problems.These outputs were coupled with automated identification of Potential Release Areas (PRA) and avalanche dynamics simulations using the AvaFrame framework, together forming PRISM (Potential Release-area & Impact Scenario Modelling), which generates daily scenario-based maps of potential release and impact areas under different instability regimes.Automatic avalanche detection systems added a real-time observational layer: a geophone-based system with traffic-light control and an infrasound array enabled continuous (24/7) detection of avalanche events, even under poor visibility or during nighttime.High-resolution webcams supported rapid validation of detected events and enhanced situational awareness.Satellite-based SAR observations (Sentinel-1) provided spatially distributed evidence of avalanche activity and supported the identification of released slopes and residual hazard areas.All data streams were integrated into dedicated operational platforms, enabling real-time visualization, analysis and reporting.The strength of the approach lies in the synergy between complementary components: observations describe current conditions, models anticipate future evolution, and remote sensing validates spatial patterns.The system was successfully tested under critical conditions during February 2026, including periods of High avalanche danger (level 4 of 5), while simultaneously managing routine avalanche forecasting and risk mitigation activities typical of an inhabited alpine valley and ski resort, demonstrating the effectiveness of an integrated observation-modelling-decision framework for avalanche risk mitigation in high-stakes environments.

title: Poland's state capitalism, state dirigisme and the European Games
title_original: Poland's state capitalism, state dirigisme and the European Games
summary: This article examines Poland's organisation of the 2023 European Games as a case study of state capitalism and dirigisme under the Law and Justice (PiS) government. Drawing on qualitative analysis of official documents, public statements and media coverage, the study examines the political rationales, institutional arrangements and discursive justifications underpinning the decision to host the Games and the political processes surrounding the project. The study analyses how illiberal governance and centralised control were exerted as the showcase of the state’s dirigisme. It argues that the Games exemplified a politically driven megaproject shaped by the pursuit of the ‘political sublime’ – the symbolic display of state efficacy rather than pragmatic legacy goals. By situating the Polish case within broader debates on mega-events and public management, the article shows that even events of relatively limited global prominence can reproduce governance patterns typically associated with the ‘flagship’ sporting mega-events like the Olympic Games or FIFA World Cups. Additional context emphasising the role of the state’s dirigisme and political sublime of sporting events emerging from the analysis concerns the fact that all major political parties in Poland, otherwise bitterly conflicted, declare that pursuing the goal of hosting, for the first time, the Summer Olympic Games in Poland is a part of their political agenda.

title: Tennis as a Spark for Olympic Health Legacy in Developing Host Cities
title_original: Tennis as a Spark for Olympic Health Legacy in Developing Host Cities
summary: Tennis as a sport, with its accessibility and comprehensive health benefits, offers a strategic chance to amplify the Olympic health legacy, especially in developing host cities. By utilizing tennis beyond elite competition, cities can foster sustainable health improvements through inclusive infrastructure, community programs, and long-term engagement. This paper explores how tennis can contribute to physical, mental, and social well-being, while also promoting public health systems and urban development through Olympic legacy frameworks.

title: Fortifying the Arena: Multi-Layered Security Strategies for the 2036 Olympics in Ahmedabad
title_original: Fortifying the Arena: Multi-Layered Security Strategies for the 2036 Olympics in Ahmedabad
summary: The Olympics and Indian Premier League (IPL), as mega-events important to the world due to their acknowledgment of athletic accomplishments and cultural cohesion, are situated to experience asymmetric and diverse threats and attacks as a result of their size and complexity. This paper examines global and technical propositions incorporated into security research, and states over fifty years of academic research and operational experiences with event and stadium security, including being an integral part of the managing of the security program at Wankhede Stadium for IPL seasons. This paper calls on the three-fold sections of security, an array of concepts, using evidence through observation and review of the mega-events of Olympic Games. This piece recommends a multi-faceted approach on behalf of the 2036 Olympics considering aspect of threat prevention, anticipating what innovation technology will be a consideration, the rapid-outlining of geospatial threat, and engaging with a stakeholders as organizations, the public and private sector professionals. In this paper is the managing and overview of formal strategies for resilience, external threat and vulnerability mitigations, as well as discussions on formal approaches urban planning, and forums designed to research a legacy of security. The review is framed with recommendations for future planning, real-time policing and constant access to data, augmented policies and by engaging with a stewardship model of governance. Mega-events like the Olympics and Indian Premier League (IPL) symbolize a global fusion of sport, culture, and technology, but their scale makes them susceptible to multi-dimensional and asymmetric threats. This paper seeks to develop a context-specific, multi-layered security framework for the proposed 2036 Olympics in Ahmedabad, India, by merging basic empirical local risk data with established best practices for the security of mega-events. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach, this research references both the forthcoming 2024 Ahmedabad Security Risk Assessment (SRA) and comparative past case studies of Olympic Games. Analytical frameworks, such as a composite risk matrix (C × D × E model) and geospatial threat mapping, are used to assess critical vulnerabilities associated with terrorism, CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear) hazards, natural disasters, and socio-political instability. The present research draws its theoretical underpinning from three different viewpoints: Beck&s;s Risk Society (1992), Foucault&s;s Panopticism (1977), and Graham and Wood&s;s Surveillance Urbanism (2003) to examine how technological systems and governance structures impact security preparedness and urban resilience. The outcomes emphasize the importance of predictive analytics, integrated command and control centers, and coordinated stakeholder engagement as the most crucial elements of threat mitigation, at the same time, preserving democratic norms and data privacy standards. This research provides a reproducible, evidence-based framework that not only aligns operational effectiveness with ethical governance but is also specifically tailored for cities in the Global South. Additionally, it points to the potential of such programs to create security legacies that deepen urban safety and resilience over time.

title: Hosting Olympic Games in Divided Nations During the Cold War Era: The Legacy of the 1972 Munich and 1988 Seoul Games
title_original: Hosting Olympic Games in Divided Nations During the Cold War Era: The Legacy of the 1972 Munich and 1988 Seoul Games
summary: This study compares the 1972 Munich and 1988 Seoul Olympics—two Games hosted by divided nations aligned with the Western bloc during the Cold War. While each event has been extensively studied in isolation, comparative research remains limited. Using a three-level framework (national, interstate, international), this paper addresses that gap by analysing the motivations, the challenges and responses, and the legacies of both cases. Findings show how each nation used the Olympics to reshape its international image, assert legitimacy, and navigate Cold War tensions. Differences in political systems—bottom-up federal democracy in West Germany and top-down authoritarianism in South Korea—shaped contrasting approaches to planning and execution. The study argues that these Games were not the culmination of national development strategies, but rather transformative junctures that redefined political narratives, urban infrastructure, international standing, and sport science in each country. This analysis contributes to Olympic historiography and offers practical insights for contemporary nations considering Olympic bids amid ongoing domestic and geopolitical challenges.

Using a three-level framework (national, interstate, international), this paper addresses that gap by analysing the motivations, the challenges and responses, and the legacies of both cases. Findings show how each nation used the Olympics to reshape its international image, assert legitimacy, and navigate Cold War tensions. Differences in political systems—bottom-up federal democracy in West Germany and top-down authoritarianism in South Korea—shaped contrasting approaches to planning and execution. The study argues that these Games were not the culmination of national development strategies, but rather transformative junctures that redefined political narratives, urban infrastructure, international standing, and sport science in each country. This analysis contributes to Olympic historiography and offers practical insights for contemporary nations considering Olympic bids amid ongoing domestic and geopolitical challenges.

title: From the Past to the Future: Environmental Legacies of the Olympic Games in a Warming World
title_original: From the Past to the Future: Environmental Legacies of the Olympic Games in a Warming World
summary: Olympic Games are considered to be one of the most impactful mega-sports events taking place after every four years. The Olympic Games stimulate the economical, social and environmental conditions of cities all over the world. Recent Olympics in Paris in 2024 caused a carbon footprint of 1.59 million teqco2, an unbelievable reduction in 54.6 percent emission over London 2012 and Rio 2016 Games. The paper is a mixed-method study, which examines the environmental legacies of the Olympic Games based on secondary data. It covers the historical analysis, comparative assessment between host cities, and provides the information on climate-responsive policies. The results indicate considerable change in carbon footprints, noting that the emissions for the 2024 Paris Games were reduced compared to previous Games, however, issues, such as greenwashing and environmental impact of mega-events, remain the same; the study indicates the need for host cities, including developing countries like India and Indonesia, to create detailed sustainability mechanisms, which will increase the longevity and legacy of the Olympic Games in a warming planet.

title: India's Quest for Hosting 2036 Olympics: Benefits, Risks and Mitigation Strategies
title_original: India's Quest for Hosting 2036 Olympics: Benefits, Risks and Mitigation Strategies
summary: The Olympic Games are the biggest sporting extravaganza and bring together billions of viewers while providing an opportunity for host nations to showcase their cultural and economic strengths. Hosting such an event presents a platform for increased economic growth, job creation, promoting tourism, and attracting foreign investment for host nations and cities. However, past host cities including Athens (2004), and Montreal (1976) have faced issues like financial burdens, unused infrastructure, and increasing debts. As India aspires to host the 2036 Olympics, this paper examines the challenges, risks, and proposes strategies necessary to host the games in a manner that&s;s economically sustainable and environmentally responsible. A narrative literature review was conducted followed by thematic analysis to assess India&s;s preparedness and propose recommendations for hosting the 2036 Olympics. It analyses secondary data sources, including reports from the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the Olympic Games Organizing Committees (OGOCs), as well as research papers and articles. The findings show that hosting the Games can have a positive impact on the economy as a result of increased tourism and foreign direct investment, generate employment opportunities, and support urban renewal through infrastructure development projects. Nonetheless, despite these potential benefits, it also poses risks like huge cost overruns, governance and corruption issues, the “white elephant phenomenon,” and security issues, all of which entail hefty costs. By employing strategic planning, promoting public- private partnerships, and strengthening governance, India can mitigate these risks and organise a successful Olympic Games that leaves a lasting legacy.

title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Olympic Security and it's Challenges
title_original: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Olympic Security and it's Challenges
summary: The modern wave of terrorist violence has also cast its shadow on the Olympics. The world&s;s biggest sporting event provides terrorist groups with a perfect platform to gain attention and create a sense of fear across countries. In the post 9/11 world, security measures have been enhanced due to the perception of heightened threat of terrorist violence. At least since the 2004 Athens Olympics, technological solutions are being explored and integrated to enhance the security of the games. China was the first country to use Artificial Intelligence for security purposes at the summer Olympics in 2008. Since then, each host country has invested significant resources in securing the games. These measures have not just increased the costs of hosting Olympics, but security related budget now constitute a significant part of the overall Olympics spending. The security and surveillance systems deployed and tested at Olympics are among its lasting legacies especially for authoritarian regimes. The reliability of the AI tools used is another challenge. States hosting must contemplate these choices when they organising the Olympics.

title: Assessing the Legacy Possibilities of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games
title_original: Assessing the Legacy Possibilities of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games
summary: The Summer Olympic Games have been held twice in Australia: 1956 in Melbourne and 2000 in Sydney. A third Olympic and Paralympic Games has been awarded to Brisbane in 2032. Using archival research which locates legacy in documents relating to both the 1956 and 2000 Olympics, this article considers how notions of legacy are being presented to the public in the years leading to Brisbane 2032. The term ‘legacy’ was first mentioned in the Melbourne candidature bid, and much more prominently in the Olympic Movement since Sydney 2000. Legacy is a result of vision, encompassing tangible and non-tangible benefits by hosting the Olympics. There are increased cultural, social, and political expectations to deliver more positive ‘legacies’ for host regions. This research also considers the role that Australia&s;s three International Olympic Committee sanctioned Centers for Olympic Studies can play in identifying and empowering opportunities for legacy creation in the lead up to the 2032 Games.

title: Avoiding White Elephants in Olympic Games: Lessons for India's 2036 Olympic Bid from Past Hosts
title_original: Avoiding White Elephants in Olympic Games: Lessons for India's 2036 Olympic Bid from Past Hosts
summary: The problem of “white elephants”—costly, underutilized Olympic infrastructure—has imposed significant financial and social burdens on numerous host cities. This study employs a comparative case study methodology to examine the post-Games legacy of Athens 2004, Sochi 2014, Rio 2016, and London 2012, focusing on legacy planning, venue utilization, economic outcomes, and community integration. Data were collected from academic literature, International Olympic Committee reports, government documents, and evaluations to assess legacy outcomes across diverse economic and cultural contexts. Findings highlight London&s;s success through proactive legacy integration, temporary venues, and urban regeneration alignment, in contrast to Athens’ neglected venues, which are due to reactive planning. Sochi&s;s ambitious infrastructure faced sustainability challenges, while Rio achieved partial success through educational and transportation initiatives, despite political disruptions. For India&s;s 2036 Olympic bid, recommendations include early legacy planning, multi-purpose venue designs, public-private partnerships, and alignment with the Smart Cities Mission. By adopting digital platforms for transparent governance and community engagement, India can avoid white elephants and establish a global benchmark for sustainable Olympic hosting.

title: Turistična izkušnja in zadovoljstvo na mega-športnih dogodkih : študija primera zimskih olimpijskih iger Milano–Cortina 2026
title_original: Turistična izkušnja in zadovoljstvo na mega-športnih dogodkih : študija primera zimskih olimpijskih iger Milano–Cortina 2026
summary: This thesis examines tourist experience and visitor satisfaction at the Milano–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games. The main aim of the study was to analyse how tourists evaluated their experiences during the event and to identify the factors that influenced their overall satisfaction. A qualitative research design was adopted, using qualitative content analysis of user-generated content based on 91 online visitor reviews collected from platforms including Google Maps, Reddit, YouTube, Business Insider, and Itinerant Fan. The findings indicate that most visitors evaluated their experience positively, highlighting the Olympic atmosphere, high-quality sporting competitions, natural Alpine scenery, volunteer support, the opportunity to explore different host destinations, and the opportunity to participate in winter sport activities themselves. At the same time, the study identified several organisational challenges related to transportation, accommodation, crowd management, food services, accessibility, and visitor information. The results demonstrate that tourist satisfaction at mega-sport events depends not only on the sporting programme but also on the quality of supporting tourism services and destination management. Based on the findings, practical recommendations are provided for organisers of future mega-sport events to improve visitor experience, event organisation, and the quality of tourism services.

title: Physical Disability Inclusion, Rights, and Representation in the North American Professional Sports Industry
title_original: Physical Disability Inclusion, Rights, and Representation in the North American Professional Sports Industry
summary: This thesis focuses on the history of physical disability inclusion, rights, and representation in the North American professional sports industry, from the early 1980s to 2026 It examines progress and resistance in furthering disability inclusion and integration in the professional sports industry among athletes, team staff, and fans. The current literature on disability within the sports industry largely focuses on the Paralympics, which means there is a substantial gap in the sport management literature. This thesis contributes to filling that gap by examining disability in professional sport. This thesis argues that the professional sports world is a helpful stage to amplify and portray disability integration, inclusion, and accommodation for athletes, fans, and team personnel, while simultaneously revealing significant barriers that remain. This thesis concludes with a discussion of major areas of improvement to further address the needs and reality of the lived disability experience within the professional North American sports industry.

title: Quebec, pioneer of Olympic education: the little-known story of the 1976 Montreal Games
title_original: Quebec, pioneer of Olympic education: the little-known story of the 1976 Montreal Games
summary: In the run-up to the 1976 Montreal Olympic Games, physical education in Quebec came under fierce criticism, with some even calling it a ‘disgrace.’ Based on this observation, this paper aims to analyze how the Olympic context served as a catalyst for redefining the role of physical education and sport in Quebec society, particularly in the field of education. The 1976 Montreal Olympic Games left a major educational legacy, often overshadowed by financial and organizational challenges. The ‘Promotion de l’Olympisme en Milieu Scolaire’ (Promotion of Olympism in Schools) program, the first of its kind, made history by integrating Olympic education into Quebec schools. Inspired by Pierre de Coubertin's humanistic vision, this program aimed to promote the values of sport and Olympism while improving the physical fitness of youth in Quebec. It served as a model for the Olympic Movement, which drew inspiration from it to develop similar initiatives on a global scale. The legacy of POMS lies in its innovative approach, combining physical education, Olympic values, and inclusion, and in its lasting impact on Quebec's sports and educational culture, which continues to this day.

It served as a model for the Olympic Movement, which drew inspiration from it to develop similar initiatives on a global scale. The legacy of POMS lies in its innovative approach, combining physical education, Olympic values, and inclusion, and in its lasting impact on Quebec's sports and educational culture, which continues to this day.

title: Resolution of Human Rights Disputes Arising from Megasport Events: Why Claims Against Sport Governing Bodies Are Next to Impossible
title_original: Resolution of Human Rights Disputes Arising from Megasport Events: Why Claims Against Sport Governing Bodies Are Next to Impossible
summary: Sport governing bodies (SGBs) such as FIFA and the International Olympic Committee absolve themselves of any liability under contract or tort from claims arising in connection with megasport events. They are able to do this by delegating all liability from potential claims to the MSE’s host state and its local organizing committee. As a result of these host state agreements, the host state will adopt enabling legislation and the SGB in question will be immune not only as a matter of contract, but also as a matter of law. This state of affairs is not satisfactory, chiefly because the SGB, as the superior negotiating party in host state agreements, has the power to impose stricter and more efficient procedures for access to justice as a form of responsibility incumbent on host states. Such responsibility may well include a rigid obligation to expeditiously and impartially subject relevant claims to standing or ad hoc judicial and arbitral bodies. In turn, these bodies must dispense justice in a manner that is consistent with fundamental human rights. This is something that SGBs have consciously failed to demand in host state agreements, thereby leaving claims by aggrieved parties unresolved or subjected to mechanisms that fail to deliver true justice. Therefore, it is imperative that the next generation of host state agreements engage with the needs of disadvantaged stakeholders and demand that host states adapt to higher standards of fair trial rights.

title: Redes geográficas musicais e festas: discussões a partir do Festival Honk! no Rio de Janeiro
title_original: Redes geográficas musicais e festas: discussões a partir do Festival Honk! no Rio de Janeiro
summary: Este trabajo investiga las redes geográficas de HONK!, un festival de bandas de música activistas en Río de Janeiro. Desde una perspectiva multiescalar, examina los procesos de intercambio cultural y carnavalización de sus actuaciones, así como las singularidades que lo permean en el contexto carioca y sus relaciones con la morfología de la ciudad. Se hace evidente que el evento, como tantos otros, se consolida como una ocasión espacial y temporal que conecta lo local y global a través de flujos que implican el desplazamiento de sujetos, conocimientos y referencias.

title: PARQUE RADICAL DE DEODORO – RIO DE JANEIRO: Características, usos no período pós-jogos e necessidades da comunidade local
title_original: PARQUE RADICAL DE DEODORO – RIO DE JANEIRO: Características, usos no período pós-jogos e necessidades da comunidade local
summary: This paper aims to investigate the characteristics of Olympic facilities, their use in the post-games period, and the needs of the local community. The research is justified by the recurring underutilization of Olympic facilities, which raises questions about urban planning and social inclusion. To meet the objective, the study was conducted at the facilities of Parque Radical, Deodoro Sports Complex, Rio de Janeiro. Questionnaires were applied to 132 users of the Deodoro Sports Complex and 108 residents of the surrounding area. In addition, 55 interviews were conducted with users of the Deodoro Sports Complex, residents of the surrounding area, and employees of Parque Radical. Quantitative data from the questionnaires were analyzed using SPSS/PC software, while the interviews were interpreted qualitatively. The results indicate that adapting the facilities for multiple uses favors access to sports and leisure, but operational barriers limit their use. The location in a vulnerable area did not guarantee integration with the community, highlighting the need for public policies to enable their continued use. The study contributes to the debate on Olympic legacies and suggests strategies to make these spaces more accessible and sustainable.

title: Sixteen Years Later: Revisiting Cultural Complexes and the Roots of Archetypal Thematic Analysis (ATA) 1
title_original: Sixteen Years Later: Revisiting Cultural Complexes and the Roots of Archetypal Thematic Analysis (ATA) 1
summary: Abstract Written as a letter to my 28‐year‐old self, this paper explores the development of my engagement with cultural complexes . On August 18, 2009, I finished a chapter applying cultural complexes to a history of China, complete with elaborate charts that seemed to confirm a process by which cultural complexes are formed, and how China’s then recent actions during the Beijing Olympic Games (i.e., utilising 7‐year‐old Yang Peiyi’s vocals yet refusing to allow her to perform at the opening ceremony, opting instead for the lip‐syncing of 9‐year‐old Lin Miaoke and the initial cover‐up of classical dancer Liu Yan’s accident during rehearsals) seemed to confirm the constellation of emotional and behavioural patterns that could be usefully assembled under the concept. While this paper is an opportunity to reflect on my critical assessment of cultural complexes, it is equally an example of autoethnographic study and a meditation on personal archival practices within a post‐ and neo‐Jungian framework. Crucially, an autoethnographic approach has facilitated an understanding of how the development of archetypal thematic analysis (ATA) (in collaboration with Ann Yeoman) stems from my thinking around, and appraisal of, cultural complexes. ATA is offered as a complement to cultural complex theory (CCT) in the hopes that a mobilisation of both can produce a methodological expression of a ‘third way’ or what Paul Preciado calls a mutant psychoanalysis .

title: Avaliação da Satisfação dos Voluntários com as Iniciativas de Sustentabilidade nos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris 2024
title_original: Avaliação da Satisfação dos Voluntários com as Iniciativas de Sustentabilidade nos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris 2024
summary: This study examines volunteer satisfaction with the sustainability initiatives implemented during the Paris 2024 Olympic Games using the psychological constructs of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as a theoretical framework. Rather than testing the original TPB model, the study investigates whether attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are associated with satisfaction across seven sustainability dimensions: Carbon Neutrality, Renewable Energy, Public Transport, Waste Management, Sustainable Architecture, Social Inclusion, and Economic Sustainability. The results reveal that subjective norms were significant positive predictors across several sustainability dimensions, highlighting the importance of social expectations in shaping volunteer evaluations. Perceived behavioral control also showed significant positive associations, particularly with Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy, suggesting that volunteers who perceived greater ability to contribute reported higher satisfaction. However, lower explanatory power was observed for Public Transport and Social Inclusion, indicating that additional contextual factors may influence volunteer satisfaction. These findings demonstrate that TPB-derived psychological constructs provide a useful perspective for understanding volunteer evaluations of sustainability initiatives and offer practical implications for enhancing volunteer experiences in future mega-sport events, consistent with the sustainability objectives of Olympic Agenda 2020+5.

title: The Price of the Games—Or Whether Mega‐Sporting Events Improve Human Rights in the Host Country
title_original: The Price of the Games—Or Whether Mega‐Sporting Events Improve Human Rights in the Host Country
summary: ABSTRACT Objective The controversy surrounding the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar and the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States has renewed debate over whether hosting mega‐sporting events affects human rights. This article examines whether host governments strategically adjust civil liberties in response to international scrutiny. Methods Using a bidder‐based difference‐in‐differences design, it analyses 74 FIFA World Cups and Olympic Games (1900–2022), comparing successful hosts with unsuccessful bidders across nine civil liberties dimensions from the Varieties of Democracy (V‐Dem) dataset. Results The findings support a selective adjustment thesis. Seven dimensions show no statistically robust effects, suggesting that hosting does not systematically alter most civil liberties. Freedom from forced labor improves before events but deteriorates afterward, consistent with strategic reputation management. A marginal effect on freedom of religion does not survive multiple‐testing correction. Conclusions Host governments, therefore, appear to selectively manage internationally visible rights rather than undertake genuine human rights reform.

title: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
title_original: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
summary: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. The deposit is hosted by carbonate- and calc-silicate-rich rocks of the Corella Formation and comprises diopside–garnet–scapolite–wollastonite ± amphibole assemblages associated with pyrrhotite–chalcopyrite–pyrite mineralisation. Field relationships and mineral textures indicate that sulphide deposition began during or shortly after prograde skarn formation and subsequently evolved from disseminated and vein-controlled to semi-massive, massive, and shear-zone-hosted mineralisation. LA-ICP-MS analyses of pyrite, pyrrhotite, chalcopyrite, and magnetite record systematic variation in trace-element compositions during this evolution. Early Py1 is enriched in Co and Se and displays Co/Sb–Se/As characteristics consistent with a magmatic-hydrothermal contribution. Se-in-pyrite thermometry yields formation temperatures of up to 544 ± 36 °C for the earliest stage, decreasing to approximately 323–417 °C in later Py1 and 342 ± 11 °C for Py2. The transition from Co-rich Py1 to Co-poor, Ni-enriched Py2, together with pyrrhotite-dominated assemblages and cross-cutting chalcopyrite–pyrrhotite textures, records progressive changes in fluid chemistry and conditions of sulphide stability. Variable magnetite trace-element compositions and brecciation further indicate repeated modification during continued fluid circulation. Structural relationships demonstrate that deformation enhanced permeability along the Mary Kathleen structural architecture, promoting fluid focusing, sulphide redistribution, and local concentration within retrograde alteration zones. We interpret Elaine Dorothy as a deformation-enhanced Paleoproterozoic calcic skarn that evolved toward a skarn–IOCG transitional system, rather than as a classic IOCG end member. The deposit demonstrates how deformation, fluid–rock interaction, and evolving redox–sulphur-fugacity conditions progressively modify an early calcic skarn framework, enhancing permeability and fluid focusing, and generating IOCG-affinity characteristics through continued hydrothermal reworking rather than a discrete IOCG-forming event. This provides a process-based framework for recognising structurally reworked skarn systems in Proterozoic mineral provinces.

The deposit demonstrates how deformation, fluid–rock interaction, and evolving redox–sulphur-fugacity conditions progressively modify an early calcic skarn framework, enhancing permeability and fluid focusing, and generating IOCG-affinity characteristics through continued hydrothermal reworking rather than a discrete IOCG-forming event. This provides a process-based framework for recognising structurally reworked skarn systems in Proterozoic mineral provinces.

title: Infographic showing the layered hierarchy of computer systems from application software down to physics.This infographic presents a top-to-bottom stack that explains how higher-level software depends on lower-level hardware and physical principles. The sections, in reading order from top to bottom, are: Application Software, Operating Systems, Architecture, Microarchitecture, Logic, Digital Circuits, Analog Circuits, Devices and Physics. Application Software includes a small code-style callout that reads greater than "hello world!". Operating Systems is paired with a laptop icon to represent the computer environment that runs applications. Architecture is illustrated with a block-like layout suggesting system organization. Microarchitecture is shown with two vertical blocks connected by two-way arrows, indicating internal data movement between components. Logic is represented by a rectangular logic block containing a plus sign. Digital Circuits is paired with a logic gate icon. Analog Circuits is paired with an operational amplifier symbol that includes plus and minus inputs. Devices is paired with a transistor-like schematic symbol. Physics is paired with an atom icon, indicating the physical foundation underlying electronic devices.Linux
