title: Virginia Woolf: dance, rhythm, movement
title_original: Virginia Woolf: dance, rhythm, movement
summary: Despite the rich cultural exchange between the arts in the late-nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, particularly between dance and literature, the study of rhythm, movement, and dance has been relatively neglected in Woolf studies. Moving beyond the current critical focus on ballet, this thesis draws on Virginia Woolf’s biographies, diaries, essays, juvenilia, letters, and novels, alongside the socio-cultural history of dance and feminist theories of the body and gendered movement, to explore how Woolf’s use of physical expression, dance, and rhythmic variation might upend orthodox masculinity, patriarchal oppression, and social class hierarchies. Chapter one looks at how Woolf employs circle- or couple-dances in The Voyage Out (1915) to explore embodiment, gender fluidity, and social control. Formally staid ballroom dance, regarded as a manifestation of patriarchy, is replaced with vibrant Bacchanalian movements that mirror modern dance’s focus on spontaneous, voluntary motion. Chapter two argues that Orlando’s ballet-inflected steps test the limits of conservative masculinity, embracing alternative forms. It goes on to consider the figure of the female Olympic ice-dancer as a possible source of inspiration for Princess Sasha Romanovich, whose fluid movement across the ice resists conformity. Chapter three delves into human/nonhuman dance-related movement in Flush: A Biography (1933), To the Lighthouse (1927) and The Waves (1931), examining how ingenious female artists breach gender boundaries by operating outside male-dominated models. Consequently, Woolf’s engagement with the nonhuman is less concerned with destabilising humanist values than with deepening her critique of gender inequality. The final chapter investigates how the foxtrot and embodied movement in The Years and Between the Acts (1941) critique social hierarchies, reflecting the novelist’s democratic response to elitism. As such, this thesis intervenes in, and contributes to, various debates in Woolf studies, offering fresh insights into Virginia Woolf’s engagement with embodiment, gender, and social politics.

title: Evaluating the usability and practicality of a proposed carbon footprint methodology and tool for National Olympic Committees
title_original: Evaluating the usability and practicality of a proposed carbon footprint methodology and tool for National Olympic Committees
summary: Robust carbon footprint methodologies and tools are increasingly required across the sport sector, yet National Olympic Committees lack a standardised, sector-specific approach. A bespoke carbon footprint methodology and accompanying calculation tool were developed for this purpose; however, technical rigour alone does not ensure that intended users can apply them. This study evaluates the usability and practicality of the proposed methodology and tool through direct engagement with end-users. Fourteen staff members from different National Olympic Committees applied the methodology and tool within their organisations over a four-to-six-week period, then completed the System Usability Scale and a semi-structured interview. The tool achieved a mean System Usability Scale score of 68.4, corresponding to a grade C and a marginal-high acceptability rating. Usability was rated positively, whereas learnability scored below the neutral midpoint, and scores correlated strongly with participants' years of experience (r = .99). Interviews indicated that effectiveness was the strongest dimension and learnability the weakest, with data collection identified as the main source of effort. Participants judged the methodology rigorous and credible but recommended improved onboarding, validation, and guidance to support less experienced users and wider adoption.

title: Professionalization of coaches in performance-oriented sport for athletes with visual impairments: a qualitative study
title_original: Professionalization of coaches in performance-oriented sport for athletes with visual impairments: a qualitative study
summary: Introduction Coaching athletes with visual impairments (VI) involves distinct pedagogical, sport-specific, and organizational demands. However, research on the professionalization of coaches in Paralympic sport remains scarce. This study explores qualifications, experiences, attitudes, and contextual conditions relevant to coaching in this setting. Methods Semi-structured expert interviews were conducted with four experienced coaches working in blind football, goalball, judo, and rowing at a German Paralympic training center. Transcripts were analyzed using structuring qualitative content analysis with an inductive–deductive category-development approach. Results Five interrelated dimensions emerged: pathways and motivations for Paralympic coaching, qualifications and competencies, coaching philosophy, institutional conditions, and sport-specific adaptations. Formal qualifications provide an important basis, but disability-specific expertise was primarily acquired through practical experience and self-directed learning. Empathy, flexible communication, individualized motor-learning strategies, and trust-based yet performance-oriented coach athlete relationships were central to practice. Limited resources, informal entry pathways, and insufficient specialist education constrained professionalization. Conclusions Coaching in performance-oriented sport for athletes with VI requires more than theory-based licenses. Practice-oriented, disability- and sport-specific education, mentoring, and the systematic transfer of experiential knowledge are needed. Stronger institutional support and collaboration among schools, clubs, and federations may promote sustainable coaching structures and equitable athlete development in Paralympic sport.

title: Ergogenic effects of beetroot juice supplementation on neuromuscular function and simulated combat demands in elite female taekwondo athletes
title_original: Ergogenic effects of beetroot juice supplementation on neuromuscular function and simulated combat demands in elite female taekwondo athletes
summary: Beetroot juice supplementation has been widely examined across various sport disciplines due to its potential ergogenic effects. However, evidence regarding its impact on combat sports particularly in female athletes remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the acute effects of beetroot juice supplementation on simulated taekwondo combat performance and neuromuscular function in elite female taekwondo athletes. Seven elite female Olympic taekwondo athletes (age: 20.3 ± 3.7 years), participated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study consisting of two experimental trials). Each trial involved the consumption of either 140 mL of beetroot juice (which contains 12.8 mmol NO₃⁻) or 140 mL of a placebo (with 0.08 mmol NO₃⁻) followed by a simulated taekwondo combat session and assessments of neuro-muscular function (i.e., vertical jump and visual cognitive performance). In addition, metabolic (i.e., blood lactate), and perceptual responses (i.e., rate of perceived exertion) were measured before, after, and 3 minutes post-combat. No significant differences during the simulated taekwondo combat (e.g., attack time; p = 0.531–0.989; ηp² = 0.01–0.05), neuromuscular function battery (p = 0.302-0.700; ηp² = 0.02-0.04), blood lactate concentrations (p = 0.705; ηp² = 0.13), or rate of perceived exertion values (RPE) (p = 0.717; ηp² = 0.12) were obtained between beetroot juice and placebo conditions. Acute ingestion of beetroot juice (140 mL) did not enhance simulated combat performance or neuromuscular function in female Olympic taekwondo athletes.

title: “The gym became a bit of a lab”: International Olympic Weightlifting coaches’ situated knowledges of training women athletes
title_original: “The gym became a bit of a lab”: International Olympic Weightlifting coaches’ situated knowledges of training women athletes
summary: In this paper, we extend gender-responsive coaching literature by examining how coaches’ learning processes influence their knowledges about sex, gender and athleticism. Our analysis draws upon semi-structured interviews with 10 coaches of elite women Olympic Weightlifters from eight countries: Aotearoa New Zealand, Botswana, Canada, China, Colombia, Denmark, the Philippines and the United States. Using Haraway’s concept of “situated knowledge”, we discuss how coaches’ knowledges were shaped by their national sport systems, gender norms within their national contexts, and their bodily experiences of Olympic Weightlifting. Exploring the contradictory understandings of women’s bodies, minds and motivations that these coaches relayed, we discuss whether any of these knowledges can be considered “better” than the others. We conclude that while coaches’ contradictory knowledges may be constructed in response to the diverse gendered bodies and identities that they encounter, they may still be critiqued based on the futures they imply for women athletes.

title: Editorial: Exploring the multidisciplinary roles of sports events
title_original: Editorial: Exploring the multidisciplinary roles of sports events
summary: The five core pillars of this topic, drawing on original empirical research and systematic reviews, illustrate the multidisciplinary complexity of the sporting landscape, namely:  The success of major sports events is fundamentally dependent on the volunteer workforce, a vital human resource that facilitates long-term social legacies. Empirical evidence from the Special Olympics World Games 2023 (SOWG 23) reveals that volunteer motivations in inclusive settings are primarily intrinsic, driven by a desire to express personal values and establish interpersonal contacts.Notably, the research identifies a parental history of volunteering as a key predictor of sustained engagement, suggesting that values instilled during childhood continue to influence active commitment well into adulthood. For sports organisations, these findings underscore the importance of shifting the recruitment focus away from extrinsic rewards toward strategies that emphasise community building and value alignment. To ensure a sustainable volunteering legacy, managers must implement di erentiated communication channels, such as digital platforms tailored to younger generations, to foster lasting engagement across diverse demographic groups. The multidisciplinary nature of sports events is also evident in how di erent stakeholders perceive quality. The case of GIMNASTRADA 2019, an international recreational gymnastics event, uses Service Quality Theory and Role Theory to demonstrate that "success" is highly subjective. The study found that the type of participation significantly influences quality ratings: while organisers and group leaders reported the highest levels of satisfaction, active gymnasts tended to have lower perceptions of service quality. This discrepancy is attributed to the "expectation-performance gap," in which active participants face greater performance pressure and have more stringent requirements for facilities and logistics. These findings suggest that sports management must move toward a tailored experience design, ensuring that the specific needs of athletes, families, and spectators are addressed separately to promote long-term loyalty and repeat participation. Sports events also serve as a "cultural battlefield" where national identity is constructed and contested. An analysis of Indonesian media narratives regarding the naturalisation of football players illustrates the tension between pragmatic nationalism and cultural essentialism. Media outlets often frame naturalised players as "national assets" who enhance international competitiveness, yet they simultaneously express scepticism about the athletes' "authenticity" and emotional ties to the nation. Drawing on the distinction between "thin citizenship" (legal recognition) and "thick citizenship" (cultural intimacy), the research shows how the media acts as a mediator of public perception. While some naturalised athletes successfully integrate by embracing local language and social initiatives, the discourse remains divided. This highlights the role of sporting events as critical sites for defining the symbolic boundaries of an "imagined community" in the era of globalised labour migration. From an economic and marketing perspective, the success of sports events is often linked to the "fit" or congruity between the event and its sponsoring brands. A metaanalytic review of 31 studies confirms that high levels of sports event-brand fit lead to positive cognitive, emotional, and behavioural responses from consumers. However, the e ectiveness of this fit is moderated by cultural contexts. In Eastern cultures, brand-event alignment is more e ective at generating emotional responses, reflecting a preference for harmony and collectivism. Conversely, in Western cultures, the fit has a stronger impact on behavioural intentions, such as purchase probability. Furthermore, the research suggests that symbolic brand responses-such as brand loyalty-are not instantaneous but require long-term sponsorship commitment and repeated interaction to bridge the "expectation gap" in consumers' minds. The final multidisciplinary lens focuses on the impact and legacy of sports events on the Quality of Life (QOL) of host communities. A scoping review of the literature indicates a significant shift from evaluating purely economic outcomes to measuring subjective well-being. While mega-events like the Olympics dominate the research, the review identifies an underexplored potential in small and mediumsized events to foster social capital and community cohesion. The findings suggest that the positive "feel-good" e ect of one-o mega-events is often temporary. In contrast, recurring participatory events (such as marathons) may o er more sustainable benefits for resident attachment and behavioural change. To advance this field, researchers advocate integrating objective measures, such as Heart Rate Variability (HRV), to complement subjective surveys and better understand the physiological mechanisms linking sports experiences to societal happiness.In conclusion, the articles in Exploring the Multidisciplinary Roles of Sports Events o er a profound and critical perspective on the role of sport in contemporary society. Collectively, they provide academics, event managers, and policymakers with practical insights and actionable tools to maximise the social legacies of sports events by understanding the intergenerational dynamics of volunteer motivation, improve service delivery through greater recognition of the role-specific expectations of diverse event participants, navigate the complex identity politics surrounding sports journalism and national team recruitment, optimise sponsorship strategies by acknowledging cultural di erences in consumer behaviour, and promote long-term societal well-being by moving beyond short-term economic metrics towards more holistic quality-of-life indicators. Taken together, the findings presented in this volume constitute a significant contribution to the ongoing dialogue on how sports events can be strategically leveraged to foster more inclusive, prosperous, and happier societies.

title: The Influence of Sleep and Autonomic Recovery on Performance in World-Class Swimmers at Major Competitions: The Qualifying Trials, World Championships, and Olympic Games
title_original: The Influence of Sleep and Autonomic Recovery on Performance in World-Class Swimmers at Major Competitions: The Qualifying Trials, World Championships, and Olympic Games
summary: Sleep deprivation is one of the main risk factors for impaired performance in elite athletes, but the changes in sleep and autonomic regulation in response to competitions of varying levels within the same Olympic year remain unknown. In this prospective, longitudinal, observational study, we monitored parameters related to sleep quality and quantity, as well as heart rate variability and resting heart rate, in a cohort of eight Olympic swimmers (n = 8) during the World Championships in Doha, the qualifying trials, and the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, using the Oura Ring Gen3 under real-world conditions throughout the pre-competition, competition, and post-competition phases of each event. The Olympic Games were the only event where sleep efficiency fell below the commonly used reference threshold of 85% during the competition phase accompanied by a reduction in the total sleep score and an increase in resting heart rate. The Olympic setting was accompanied by temporary changes in sleep and autonomic markers, but no sleep parameter or autonomic marker showed a statistically significant association with intra-individual competitive performance, although the limited sample size constrains the power to detect such relationships.

title: Finnish press and the societal issues of mega-sport events: a discourse analysis of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Summer Olympics
title_original: Finnish press and the societal issues of mega-sport events: a discourse analysis of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Summer Olympics
summary: Sports journalism has been criticized for ignoring sport’s social dimensions, but research suggests that those days of pure enthusiasm are over. This study inves­tigates how the Finnish press has covered societal issues in Olympic reporting and how this coverage has evolved over time. The data consist of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Olympics. Societal issues were addressed in both cases, but the proportion of such articles was higher in 2024. Applying critical discourse analysis, the study examines the discourses through which the Olympics are rep­resented in these articles. Through discourse analysis, four discourses that both question and reinforce the legitimacy of the Olympics were identified. Coverage also includes highly critical reporting of the Olympic Movement. However, the comparison demonstrates a shift toward more critical, multi-voiced, and socially reflective sports journalism. Yet, national loyalty and the pursuit of Olympic success continue to temper its critical depth.
abstract: Sports journalism has been criticized for ignoring sport’s social dimensions, but research suggests that those days of pure enthusiasm are over. This study inves­tigates how the Finnish press has covered societal issues in Olympic reporting and how this coverage has evolved over time. The data consist of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Olympics. Societal issues were addressed in both cases, but the proportion of such articles was higher in 2024. Applying critical discourse analysis, the study examines the discourses through which the Olympics are rep­resented in these articles. Through discourse analysis, four discourses that both question and reinforce the legitimacy of the Olympics were identified. Coverage also includes highly critical reporting of the Olympic Movement. However, the comparison demonstrates a shift toward more critical, multi-voiced, and socially reflective sports journalism. Yet, national loyalty and the pursuit of Olympic success continue to temper its critical depth.

title: Effects of pacing strategy on performance and physiological responses in a simulated 1000-m kayak race under the new Olympic schedule
title_original: Effects of pacing strategy on performance and physiological responses in a simulated 1000-m kayak race under the new Olympic schedule
summary: Purpose: This study examined whether adding an all-out start (AO) to a self-paced strategy increased average power outputas a measure of performance in a fixed-duration 4-min kayak ergometer trial simulating a 1000-m kayak race under the newOlympic canoe sprint schedule, and whether this pacing modification altered physiological responses.Methods: Nine national-level male kayakers completed three 4-min kayak-ergometer trials over two consecutive days: a selfpaced (SP) trial on day 1, and even-paced (EP) and AO trials on day 2 separated by 2 hours to simulate semifinal and final,respectively. In EP, athletes matched the average power output (PO) from SP; in AO, they performed a 15-s maximal effortfollowed by self-paced paddling. Mechanical and physiological variables, including PO, stroke rate, oxygen uptake, heart rate(HR), blood lactate, and acid-base parameters, were measured. Data were analyzed with frequentist and Bayesian repeatedmeasures ANOVA.Results: Compared with SP, AO produced higher average PO (194 ± 14 vs 185 ± 22 W; P = .027; BF₁₀ = 1.82) and peak HR(195 ± 4 vs 192 ± 3 beats/min; P = .045; BF₁₀ = 4.22), although the HR difference lay within typical day-to-day variability.The remaining physiological variables did not differ between strategies (all P > .35), with Bayes factors (BF₁₀ = 0.25–0.43)providing anecdotal to moderate evidence for the null model.Conclusions: A 15-s all-out start superimposed on a self-paced strategy may increase average power output during a fixedduration 4-min kayak ergometer trial under the Olympic regatta schedule without increasing physiological strain. title: Understanding athlete experiences in 3×3 basketball: a latent class analysis of service quality and satisfaction profiles
title_original: Understanding athlete experiences in 3×3 basketball: a latent class analysis of service quality and satisfaction profiles
summary: Introduction: The rapid global expansion of 3×3 basketball has transformed the sport into one of the most accessible and socially engaging forms of urban recreation. Despite its increasing popularity and inclusion in the Olympic Games, limited research has examined how participants evaluate their experiences in organized 3×3 basketball tournaments and whether distinct groups of athletes can be identified according to their perceptions of service quality and satisfaction. Objective: The purpose of this study was to identify latent athlete profiles based on perceptions of satisfaction, facilities, personnel, responsiveness, reliability, and participation outcomes in 3×3 basketball tournaments. Additionally, the study examined whether demographic and experiential characteristics, including age, years of team participation, coaching experience, and years of involvement in basketball, predicted membership in the identified profiles. Methodology: A total of 300 athletes participating in official 3×3 basketball tournaments across Greece completed validated questionnaires assessing service quality and satisfaction dimensions. Latent Class Analysis (LCA) was employed to identify homogeneous participant profiles, while demographic and experiential variables were incorporated as covariates. Results: The findings revealed three distinct athlete profiles. The first profile, labelled Low Evaluation of 3×3 (44.97%), was characterized by low levels of satisfaction and unfavorable evaluations across all service quality dimensions. The second profile, Moderate Evaluation of 3×3 (31.44%), demonstrated moderate perceptions across all variables. The third profile, High Evaluation of 3×3 (23.59%), reported consistently high levels of satisfaction, service quality perceptions, and participation outcomes. Among the examined covariates, only coaching experience significantly predicted profile membership, whereas age, years of team participation, and years of involvement in basketball were not significant predictors. Discussion: The study provides novel evidence regarding the heterogeneous nature of athlete experiences in 3×3 basketball and highlights the usefulness of person-centered analytical approaches in sport management research. Conclusion: The findings offer practical implications for event organizers, sport federations, and local authorities seeking to enhance participant experiences, increase satisfaction, and strengthen long-term engagement in urban sport events.

title: 詩讚姚明與他的「明朝」Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
title_original: 詩讚姚明與他的「明朝」Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
summary: 王抗曝、曹恆平(2026)《詩讚姚明與他的「明朝」》,《科學、技術、工程、藝術與數學之前瞻進展》, 8(10A),2026年10月,102頁,蘭諾出版社,美國麻省。Wang, Lawrence K. and Tsao, Hung-ping (2026). Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty." Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics, 8(10A), October 2026, 102 pp. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. ABSTRACT: 姚明被世界公認為中國所培育出的最傑出籃球運動員之一;然而,他長遠的歷史意義,早已超越其非凡身高與運動成就。姚明於1980年出生於上海,從上海大鯊魚隊走向國際,並於2002年成為美國國家籃球協會選秀大會的第一順位球員。在效力休士頓火箭隊期間,他八次入選NBA全明星賽,五次入選NBA最佳陣容。他曾代表中國參加三屆奧林匹克運動會,於2016年入選奈史密斯籃球名人堂,並於2023年入選國際籃球總會名人堂。本文並非一篇普通的體育人物傳記,而是一篇跨領域的生命書寫。其創作緣起,是兩位作者王抗曝博士與曹恆平博士多年來共同對姚明所懷抱的欣賞與敬意。數學家曹恆平現居加州,人道環境工程師王抗曝現居紐約;兩人曾同為臺北國立臺灣師範大學附屬高級中學同學,並各自取得四個學位,一生重視教育。他們特別敬佩姚明在傷病結束籃球生涯後,仍努力取得經濟學學士學位。受到姚明充滿意義的「第二人生」啟發,曹、王二人亦於晚年走進詩歌,成為「半路出家」的詩歌學徒。本文探討姚明從上海走向休士頓的人生旅程、籃球成就、傷痛與退役、教育、慈善、兒童體育、野生動物保育、中國籃球領導工作,以及他作為中美文化橋樑的意義。本文主張:姚明的身高使他引人注目,球技使他享譽世界,而他的堅韌、謙遜、求知、慈愛與公共服務,才使他成為真正的巨人。本文透過個人回憶、人道環境反思與三語詩章,將姚明描繪為一位第二人生遠遠超越籃球場的楷模。本書繁體中文版並非已出版英文版的單純翻譯,而是一部經過實質擴充的增訂版本。除第3.2節外,全書各章原由王抗曝博士撰寫,並已以英文版出版。曹恆平博士閱讀該英文版後,將其於2002至2008年間隨姚明NBA生涯發展而撰寫的二十六篇球評與札記交予王抗曝。這些同時代文字記錄了一位海外華人資深球迷對姚明球技、人格、傷病、國家責任及北京奧運的即時觀察、預測與憂慮。兩位作者其後共同整理、擴充及修訂這批歷史資料,使當年的現場聲音與今日的生命回望,在本增訂中文版中彼此相遇。本書結合傳記敘事、同時代球評、個人回憶、人道環境反思與三語詩章,呈現姚明從上海走向休士頓、從「大明元年」走向北京奧運,以及從籃球巨星走向教育、慈善、保育與公共服務第二人生的完整歷程。本書所稱姚明的「明朝」,並非指中國歷史上的明王朝,而是曹恆平巧妙借用姚明姓名中的「明」字,將姚明於2002年進入NBA稱為「大明元年」,並以「大明王朝」象徵海外華人球迷對其籃球生涯所寄予的期待。ABSTRACT: Yao Ming is remembered internationally as one of the greatest basketball players to emerge from China, but his enduring significance reaches far beyond his extraordinary height and athletic accomplishments. Born in Shanghai in 1980, Yao rose from the Shanghai Sharks to become the first overall selection in the 2002 National Basketball Association Draft. During his career with the Houston Rockets, he became an eight-time NBA All-Star and five-time All-NBA selection. He represented China at three Olympic Games, entered the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, and was inducted into the NBA Hall of Fame in 2023. This article is not a conventional sports biography. It is an interdisciplinary work of life writing inspired by the longtime admiration shared by the two coauthors, Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and Dr. Hung-ping Tsao, who are lifelong friends and former high-school classmates. It examines Yao's journey from Shanghai to Houston, his basketball accomplishments, physical suffering and retirement, education, philanthropy, youth programs, wildlife conservation, leadership of Chinese basketball, and role as a cultural bridge between China and the United States. Personal recollection, humanitarian environmental reflection, and trilingual poetry present Yao Ming as a role model whose second life reached far beyond the basketball court. The traditional Chinese edition of this book is not a mere translation of the already published English version; rather, it is a substantively expanded and revised edition. Except for Section 3.2, all chapters were originally written by Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and published its English edition. After reading the English edition, Dr. Hung ping Tsao entrusted Wang with twenty six commentaries and notes he had written between 2002 and 2008 during the unfolding of Yao Ming's NBA career. These contemporaneous writings document a seasoned overseas Chinese basketball fan's real time observations, predictions, and concerns regarding Yao Ming's skills, character, injuries, sense of national responsibility, and the Beijing Olympics. The two authors subsequently organized, expanded, and revised this historical corpus, allowing the voices of that era and today's reflective perspectives to meet within this enriched Chinese edition. This book weaves together biographical narrative, contemporaneous basketball commentary, personal recollection, humanitarian and environmental reflection, and trilingual poetic chapters. It presents Yao Ming's full journey—from Shanghai to Houston, from the "First Year of the Ming Era" to the Beijing Olympics, and from basketball superstar to a second life devoted to education, philanthropy, conservation, and public service. The term "Ming Dynasty" in this book does not refer to the historical Chinese dynasty; rather, Dr. Tsao ingeniously borrows the character "Ming" from Yao Ming's name, designating his entry into the NBA in 2002 as the "First Year of the Ming Era," with the "Ming Dynasty" symbolizing the hopes placed upon his basketball career by overseas Chinese fans.

Wang and Dr. Hung-ping Tsao, who are lifelong friends and former high-school classmates. Except for Section 3.2, all chapters were originally written by Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and published its English edition. These contemporaneous writings document a seasoned overseas Chinese basketball fan's real time observations, predictions, and concerns regarding Yao Ming's skills, character, injuries, sense of national responsibility, and the Beijing Olympics. The two authors subsequently organized, expanded, and revised this historical corpus, allowing the voices of that era and today's reflective perspectives to meet within this enriched Chinese edition. This book weaves together biographical narrative, contemporaneous basketball commentary, personal recollection, humanitarian and environmental reflection, and trilingual poetic chapters. It presents Yao Ming's full journey—from Shanghai to Houston, from the "First Year of the Ming Era" to the Beijing Olympics, and from basketball superstar to a second life devoted to education, philanthropy, conservation, and public service. The term "Ming Dynasty" in this book does not refer to the historical Chinese dynasty; rather, Dr. Tsao ingeniously borrows the character "Ming" from Yao Ming's name, designating his entry into the NBA in 2002 as the "First Year of the Ming Era," with the "Ming Dynasty" symbolizing the hopes placed upon his basketball career by overseas Chinese fans.

title: How do we teach English under the waves of innovation?: discovering perceptions of English learning and teaching in China and the UK
title_original: How do we teach English under the waves of innovation?: discovering perceptions of English learning and teaching in China and the UK
summary: In response to a growing amount of Chinese students pursuing higher education abroad influenced by the rapid economic, social and cultural development in China, this study explores Chinese Second Language (L2) learners and teachers’ perceptions of English Language Teaching (ELT) from secondary school level through tertiary level. English language education has experienced extensive reforms and development, however, Chinese students’ voices reflecting their English learning experience are not positioned as key consideration throughout these learning stages. In this case, this study discusses L2 learners and teachers’ experience of transitions in ELT throughout different learning stages and perceptions of intercultural knowledge embedded within ELT, uncovering English learning difficulties via self-assessment, digging deeply about L2 learners and teachers’ feedback about group work, learner autonomy, exams and interaction between students and teachers. By prioritizing learners and teachers’ feedback and hearing their voices, this study draws upon large-scale data derived from semi-structured individual and group interviews, surveys and focus groups collected over a period of 20 months’ data fieldwork in China and the UK. Responses were gathered from 500 high school students and qualitative interviews with 80 Chinese undergraduates, postgraduates and teachers in Chinese and UK universities in order to build the bridge between learning and teaching perspectives. In this study, survey and interview data is analysed to examine more specifically, Chinese undergraduates and postgraduates who are currently studying in UK universities, with particular reference to international students’ psychological and sociocultural adaptation within their visited country education systems. Specifically, key findings of this research reveal the unbalanced and unequal distribution of ELT education resources between developed and less developed regions, which closely related to students’ attitudes and awareness of output (writing and speaking) practices and access to intercultural knowledge. The influences of Confucianism and traditional Chinese learning culture on Chinese students’ English language learning, which lead to students’ fear of making mistakes and losing face. The directional and leading role of exams throughout Chinese students’ English learning journey and students’ highlights of exam strategies and memorization. The findings from this study help to shed light on how English language policies directly and indirectly influence ELT development in China.

English language education has experienced extensive reforms and development, however, Chinese students’ voices reflecting their English learning experience are not positioned as key consideration throughout these learning stages. In this case, this study discusses L2 learners and teachers’ experience of transitions in ELT throughout different learning stages and perceptions of intercultural knowledge embedded within ELT, uncovering English learning difficulties via self-assessment, digging deeply about L2 learners and teachers’ feedback about group work, learner autonomy, exams and interaction between students and teachers. By prioritizing learners and teachers’ feedback and hearing their voices, this study draws upon large-scale data derived from semi-structured individual and group interviews, surveys and focus groups collected over a period of 20 months’ data fieldwork in China and the UK. Responses were gathered from 500 high school students and qualitative interviews with 80 Chinese undergraduates, postgraduates and teachers in Chinese and UK universities in order to build the bridge between learning and teaching perspectives. In this study, survey and interview data is analysed to examine more specifically, Chinese undergraduates and postgraduates who are currently studying in UK universities, with particular reference to international students’ psychological and sociocultural adaptation within their visited country education systems. Specifically, key findings of this research reveal the unbalanced and unequal distribution of ELT education resources between developed and less developed regions, which closely related to students’ attitudes and awareness of output (writing and speaking) practices and access to intercultural knowledge. The influences of Confucianism and traditional Chinese learning culture on Chinese students’ English language learning, which lead to students’ fear of making mistakes and losing face. The directional and leading role of exams throughout Chinese students’ English learning journey and students’ highlights of exam strategies and memorization. The findings from this study help to shed light on how English language policies directly and indirectly influence ELT development in China.

title: Orphaned by an Evidentiary Standard: How Efficacy Review Emptied the Anabolic‐Androgenic Steroid Market, and What Doping Control Inherited
title_original: Orphaned by an Evidentiary Standard: How Efficacy Review Emptied the Anabolic‐Androgenic Steroid Market, and What Doping Control Inherited
summary: The anabolic-androgenic steroids have largely left clinical medicine while remaining in wide non-medical use. This review documents how that happened from the supply side, using the US Federal Register from 1970 to 2026, approval and patent records, statutes, treaty texts, and the peer-reviewed analytical literature. Three European firms created the class in 1935, their research contracted to university laboratories, and seven firms in five countries built it out by 1962, into a market where branded androgen preparations were already sold. The FDA's Drug Efficacy Study Implementation 7630 then condemned the tissue-building claims in 1970, retained an osteoporosis claim only while no alternative existed, and closed in 1985 after no sponsor completed the studies. A parallel proceeding on the estrogen-androgen combinations, opened in 1972, was resolved only in 2026. No safety finding drove any of it. Only one product in the class, oxandrolone, was ever determined withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness, and 21 CFR 216.24 contains no anabolic-androgenic steroid. Most applications lapsed. The two jurisdictions then diverged. The US moved these substances into narcotics law in 1990 while European states did not make that move, with consequences for the public health work possible in each. Three of the first designer steroids identified in sport had never been sold as medicines, and for two of them the laboratories had to synthesize reference material before any assay existed. Section S0 of the WADA Prohibited List now names discontinued drugs. The pattern has since repeated with the selective androgen receptor modulators.

title: 诗赞姚明与他的"明朝" Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
title_original: 诗赞姚明与他的"明朝" Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty"
summary: 王抗曝、曹恒平(2026)《诗赞姚明与他的"明朝"》,《科学、技术、工程、艺术与数学之前瞻进展》, 8(10B),2026年10月,102页,兰诺出版社,美国麻省。Wang, Lawrence K. and Tsao, Hung-ping (2026). Poetic Admiration for Yao Ming and His Basketball "Ming Dynasty." Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics, 8(10B), October 2026, 102 pp. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. 摘要: 《诗赞姚明与他的"明朝"》姚明被世界公认为中国所培养出的最杰出篮球运动员之一;然而,他长远的历史意义,早已超越其非凡身高与运动成就。姚明于1980年出生于上海,从上海大鲨鱼队走向国际,并于2002年成为美国国家篮球协会选秀大会的第一顺位球员。在效力休斯敦火箭队期间,他八次入选NBA全明星赛,五次入选NBA最佳阵容。他曾代表中国参加三届奥林匹克运动会,于2016年入选奈史密斯篮球名人堂,并于2023年入选国际篮球联合会名人堂。本文并非一篇普通的体育人物传记,而是一篇跨领域的生命书写。其创作缘起,是两位作者王抗曝博士与曹恒平博士多年来共同对姚明所怀抱的欣赏与敬意。数学家曹恒平现居加州,人道环境工程师王抗曝现居纽约;两人曾同为台北国立台湾师范大学附属高级中学同学,并各自取得四个学位,一生重视教育。他们特别敬佩姚明在伤病结束篮球生涯后,仍努力取得经济学学士学位。受到姚明充满意义的"第二人生"启发,曹、王二人亦于晚年走进诗歌,成为"半路出家"的诗歌学徒。本文探讨姚明从上海走向休斯敦的人生旅程、篮球成就、伤痛与退役、教育、慈善、儿童体育、野生动物保护、中国篮球领导工作,以及他作为中美文化桥梁的意义。本文主张:姚明的身高使他引人注目,球技使他享誉世界,而他的坚韧、谦逊、求知、慈爱与公共服务,才使他成为真正的巨人。本文通过个人回忆、人道环境反思与三语诗章,将姚明描绘为一位第二人生远远超越篮球场的楷模。本书简体中文版以增订繁体中文版为依据,并非已出版英文版的单纯翻译,而是一部经过实质扩充的增订版本。除第3.2节外,全书各章原由王抗曝博士撰写,并已出版。曹恒平博士阅读该英文版后,将其于2002至2008年间随姚明NBA生涯发展而撰写的二十六篇球评与札记交予王抗曝。这些同时代文字记录了一位海外华人资深球迷对姚明球技、人格、伤病、国家责任及北京奥运的即时观察、预测与忧虑。两位作者其后共同整理、扩充及修订这批历史资料,使当年的现场声音与今日的生命回望,在本增订中文版中彼此相遇。本书结合传记叙事、同时代球评、个人回忆、人道环境反思与三语诗章,呈现姚明从上海走向休斯敦、从"大明元年"走向北京奥运,以及从篮球巨星走向教育、慈善、保育与公共服务第二人生的完整历程。本书所称姚明的"明朝",并非指中国历史上的明王朝,而是曹恒平巧妙借用姚明姓名中的"明"字,将姚明于2002年进入NBA称为"大明元年",并以"大明王朝"象征海外华人球迷对其篮球生涯所寄予的期待。ABSTRACT: Yao Ming is remembered internationally as one of the greatest basketball players to emerge from China, but his enduring significance reaches far beyond his extraordinary height and athletic accomplishments. Born in Shanghai in 1980, Yao rose from the Shanghai Sharks to become the first overall selection in the 2002 National Basketball Association Draft. During his career with the Houston Rockets, he became an eight-time NBA All-Star and five-time All-NBA selection. He represented China at three Olympic Games, entered the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, and was inducted into the NBA Hall of Fame in 2023. This article is not a conventional sports biography. It is an interdisciplinary work of life writing inspired by the longtime admiration shared by the two coauthors, Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and Dr. Hung-ping Tsao, who are lifelong friends and former high-school classmates. It examines Yao's journey from Shanghai to Houston, his basketball accomplishments, physical suffering and retirement, education, philanthropy, youth programs, wildlife conservation, leadership of Chinese basketball, and role as a cultural bridge between China and the United States. Personal recollection, humanitarian environmental reflection, and trilingual poetry present Yao Ming as a role model whose second life reached far beyond the basketball court. This Simplified Chinese edition is based on the expanded Traditional Chinese edition and is not a mere translation of the already published English version; rather, it is a substantively expanded and revised edition. Except for Section 3.2, all chapters were originally written by Dr. Lawrence K. Wang and published as the English edition. After reading the English edition, Dr. Hung ping Tsao entrusted Wang with twenty six commentaries and notes he had written between 2002 and 2008 during the unfolding of Yao Ming's NBA career. These contemporaneous writings document a seasoned overseas Chinese basketball fan's real time observations, predictions, and concerns regarding Yao Ming's skills, character, injuries, sense of national responsibility, and the Beijing Olympics. The two authors subsequently organized, expanded, and revised this historical corpus, allowing the voices of that era and today's reflective perspectives to meet within this enriched Chinese edition. This book weaves together biographical narrative, contemporaneous basketball commentary, personal recollection, humanitarian and environmental reflection, and trilingual poetic chapters. It presents Yao Ming's full journey—from Shanghai to Houston, from the "First Year of the Ming Era" to the Beijing Olympics, and from basketball superstar to a second life devoted to education, philanthropy, conservation, and public service. The term "Ming Dynasty" in this book does not refer to the historical Chinese dynasty; rather, Dr. Tsao ingeniously borrows the character "Ming" from Yao Ming's name, designating his entry into the NBA in 2002 as the "First Year of the Ming Era," with the "Ming Dynasty" symbolizing the hopes placed upon his basketball career by overseas Chinese fans.

title: Technical and Operational Assessment of a Large-Scale Hydrogen Mobility System Under Extreme Winter Conditions: Evidence from the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
title_original: Technical and Operational Assessment of a Large-Scale Hydrogen Mobility System Under Extreme Winter Conditions: Evidence from the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
summary: As the decarbonisation of transport continues, hydrogen fuel cell vehicles (HFCVs) are attracting increasing attention, particularly in heavy-duty and high-utilisation applications where long operating ranges and rapid refuelling are required. Transferring HFCVs from individual demonstrations to large-scale fleet operation, however, depends on the joint performance of vehicles, hydrogen supply, refuelling infrastructure and operational management. Our study examines the technical and operational feasibility of large-scale hydrogen mobility using the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games as a case study. The analysis covers vehicle deployment and scenario matching, hydrogen production and road distribution, refuelling infrastructure, digital monitoring, fleet coordination, and operational performance under extreme winter and mountainous conditions. More than 1200 HFCVs operated for 52 days across over 80 routes and accumulated more than 3.5 million vehicle-kilometres, supported by 11 hydrogen refuelling stations and approximately 20 t d−1 of hydrogen production capacity. The case study shows that successful fleet operation depended on matching vehicle configurations to transport tasks, coordinating hydrogen supply with refuelling demand, maintaining redundancy across the supply network - and integrating real time monitoring with fleet dispatch. These findings help to identify the main technical and operational conditions for large-scale hydrogen mobility and provide practical guidance for centralised applications, such as public transport, shuttle services and logistics fleets.

title: Infrastructure-Superstructure Contradictions in Vietnamese Elite Sports: An Analysis from the Perspective of Historical Materialism
title_original: Infrastructure-Superstructure Contradictions in Vietnamese Elite Sports: An Analysis from the Perspective of Historical Materialism
summary: Applying the historical materialist principle of the dialectical relationship between infrastructure and superstructure, this study examines the development of Vietnamese elite sports from 2011 to 2026. Using historical-logical analysis and an empirical survey of managers, coaches, and athletes, the study identifies a performance paradox: Vietnam has maintained strong results at the SEA Games while achieving more limited outcomes at the ASIAD and Olympic levels. The analysis associates this pattern with institutional desynchronization between changing economic and material conditions and slower administrative and regulatory adaptation. Key issues include barriers to public-private partnerships, limited autonomy of sports federations, shortcomings in athlete remuneration and occupational insurance, and insufficient investment in advanced training technologies. In relation to Decision No. 1189/QD-TTg and national sports development objectives to 2030 with a vision to 2045, the study proposes coordinated institutional reforms, improved resource mobilization, and greater application of artificial intelligence, biosensors, and sports biomedicine to support sustainable elite sports development.

title: 33rd SEA Games Takeaways: Balancing Sport and Southeast Asia’s Complex Environment
title_original: 33rd SEA Games Takeaways: Balancing Sport and Southeast Asia’s Complex Environment
summary: The SEA Games this year took place in Thailand, marking the seventh time that the country has hosted Southeast Asia's biggest sporting event. Thailand comes out on top of the table, achieving an all-time record of 233 out of 573 possible Gold Medals, overtaking Vietnam's 2022 record of 205 Gold Medals. Another interesting fact regarding this year's event is that several countries sent their largest-ever delegations to the 33rd SEA Games as Singapore sent 930, the Philippines with 1,168, and Malaysia with 1,166 athletes, positively reflecting the expanded 50-sport program and Olympic-aligned events in this year's SEA Games. Despite the positive updates from the 33rd SEA Games, the event also saw Cambodia withdraw 1,515 athletes due to the intensifying Cambodian-Thai border conflict, leaving only 10 countries participating. In this sense, the event mirrored broader ASEAN challenges in managing intra-regional disputes while upholding the principle of regional harmony. A setback also occurred during the preparation, as cyclone Senyar hit and caused flooding in the Songkhla province, forcing 10 sports to relocate from the Southern venue just a week before the opening on 9th December 2025. Some technical issues by the organiser also coloured this year's event, including flag and national anthem errors, which raised questions about the host's preparedness. In Southeast Asia, where national identity and sovereignty remain deeply salient, such incidents risk diplomatic friction and public backlash, emphasizing the political sensitivity embedded in regional sporting events.Our adjunct researcher, Dr Muhammad Rum, delivered his point of view in accordance with the 33rd SEA Games and what lessons learned can be taken for Malaysia as the next host in 2027.

title: Sport Motivation Among Young Fencers Training in a Ukrainian Olympic Reserve School During Wartime: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
title_original: Sport Motivation Among Young Fencers Training in a Ukrainian Olympic Reserve School During Wartime: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
summary: Background and purpose Young athletes in Ukraine continue to train during the war, which may disrupt training routines and affect their motivation. However, evidence on sport motivation among young athletes training in Olympic reserve systems during wartime remains limited. This study examined motivation among young fencers training in a Ukrainian Olympic reserve school during wartime and its associations with perceived coach support and war-related disruption of training. Material and methods This exploratory cross-sectional study involved 64 young fencers from a Specialized Youth Sports School of Olympic Reserve in Mykolaiv, Ukraine. title: Editorial: Sport governance: challenges, developments and future pathways
title_original: Editorial: Sport governance: challenges, developments and future pathways
summary: Emerging challenges, including corruption scandals in sport and debates surrounding gender transition, have renewed attention on the importance of effective sport governance-the central theme of this special issue of Frontiers in Sports and Active Living. The issue consists of 13 papers that deal with a wide range of important topics across several countries, including Australia, the USA, Germany, China, Korea, Tunisia and Portugal. Although the various articles may overlap or intertwine, given the broad scope of sport governance, they can possibly be classified or categorized around six major themes based on their particular focus. These include: state involvement in sport, the Olympics, athlete development, corporate Governance, intellectual property rights and sport for development.The state-oriented articles deal with the issues of public subsidies for professional soccer in Germany, sport policy development in Australia, state intervention in US College Sports and local government in China and Portugal. In their study entitled "Public Subsidies for Professional Football Clubs: A Conceptual Political Economy Analysis," Baumeister et al. provided a more integrated conceptual framework to better understand the critical importance of state subsidies in professional football based on a study of Germany's Bundesliga. In making a case for such public subsidies, they strongly suggest that they should not be narrowly conceived as just a strategy to rescue clubs in crisis but as part of a broader sustainable developmental strategy or catalyst to promote urban development, economic growth, social cohesion, and community identity or identity formation as a whole (McCree, 2008).With respect to the USA, Hawkins interrogates the socio-political significance or fallout of one of Donald Trump's many Executive Orders (EO), in his article entitled, "Donald Trump's Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) Executive Order: A Neo-Jacksonianism Tradition." While the EO was seen as impacting all athletes in the major revenue-generating sports of American football and basketball, it was seen as having a disproportionate impact on black students who dominate participation in these two sports, which serves to reinforce the broader racialized status quo.Theoretically, the paper makes an important contribution to the study of populism in sport and populism in general and methodologically, to the use of qualitative research in sport through the application of contextual analysis. In the paper, "Australian Sport Policy and Advocacy: An Historical Account of Policy Evolution, Government Involvement, and the Advent of Lobbying," Mountifield examines the Australian state's transition from a limited role in sport to a more active and interventionist one through the creation of formal sport policies, government sport bureaucracies, ministries and ministers responsible for sport, and dedicated funding for both elite and mass sport. The paper makes an important contribution to the literature on sport policy as well as the role of advocacy or lobbying in the policy process. Three of the papers examined dealt with the Olympic Games as they relate particularly to the IOC, Olympic values and the impact of Olympic hosting on athlete performance. In their unprecedented historical examination of "The evolution of IOC membership and governance" from 1894 to 2023, Xu and Shi show how both internal and external factors of an economic, political, ideological, social and organizational nature combined to bring about substantive changes in the composition and operations of the IOC. As a consequence, the IOC has become much less Eurocentric, more meritocratic and representative, in relation to the presence of women, developing nations and athletes, although the authors question whether some of these changes, particularly the involvement of athletes, are more symbolic or cosmetic than real. In the article, "Beyond excellence, friendship and respect: Olympic education stakeholders' priorities for values in a changing world," Theodorakis et al. examine how Olympic education stakeholders recognise and seek to further contemporary values including peace, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and gender equality, in addition to the traditional Olympic values of excellence, friendship, and respect. This study is highly relevant to sports governance as it helps to see how shifts in society shape attitudes within the major sports movement, similar to the paper by Xu and Shi.In their paper entitled "Beyond the Podium: The Long-Term Impact of Hosting the Olympic Games on National Sporting Performance," Schoettl and Kainz shift from issues of values and representation to the relationship between hosting and medal outcomes. In this regard, they argue that Olympic hosting should be understood not merely as a short-term home advantage but as a strategic instrument of sports policy. The study contributes to the literature by showing that Olympic hosting can work as a policy lever whose benefits are shaped by governance capacity, strategic prioritization, and sustained investment rather than by the event itself. The article by Guidotti et al entitled "Sustainability of top-performance athletes' mental health and career retirement support services: European major sports organizations' perspective" examines much broader and important issues related to the (non)provision of formal support mechanisms, both financially and emotionally, to athletes in order to help them deal with life after sports. They argue that the available services in Europe are directed primarily towards the medal winners, which leaves a significant number of athletes outside the purview of support. This study signals an emerging trend of recognition for mental health support for elite athletes. Kwon's paper entitled "Athlete Data Sovereignty" examines the equally important issue of who owns and controls the performance data produced by athletes during training or competition (e.g., heart rate output, reaction times). Reminiscent of Marx's notion of the alienation of workers from their own labour, it is argued that since such data are an extension of the athletes' identity and not some impersonal external output, they should be allowed to exercise greater sovereignty over them.The paper assumes great relevance in the age of AI and complements the issue of athlete representation raised by Xu and Chi in their paper on the IOC. In their paper entitled "Whose game is it anyway? Palworld and the new frontier of intellectual property in eSports," Vargas-Chaves et al also deal with the issue of property rights but in the particular context of e-sports or digital sports. Through the Palworld case, especially its perceived similarities with Pokémon, the article examined the tension between creative inspiration and infringement, while distinguishing between copyright, patent protection, trademarks, and Trade Dress. This article elucidates that legal regulation, platform governance, and intellectual property management are now central to the sustainability and integrity of the eSports industry.In the only paper that focuses on national sport organizations, Ghodhbani and Souissi explore different governance models in the context of non-profit sports Federations in Tunisia in their article, "Governance of Tunisian sports organizations: what is the matter?" They argue that these Federations work within the oversight of both supranational and national regulatory systems that allow for both possibilities and constrictions. Majorly, they show how different governance models such as the strong presidential model, the couple's presidential model, the exploded presidential model, and the managerial presidential model influence the functioning of the Federations.The paper by Westerbeek et al. can be situated more in the context of sport for development due to its focus on "The costs of participation in and delivery of community sport in Australia." Based on a rigorous scoping or narrative review, the authors identify the economic and non-economic barriers to participation in community sport in Australia, critically examine existing strategies to deal with them and make several important policy recommendations to facilitate more participation. The paper should make an important contribution to the literature on sport policy as well as the growing field of sport for development.

title: “Las sirenas mexicanas” and “Las guerreras del agua”: Metaphors used in digital news from Mexican and Spanish sports newspapers
title_original: “Las sirenas mexicanas” and “Las guerreras del agua”: Metaphors used in digital news from Mexican and Spanish sports newspapers
summary: This article aims to identify the most frequently employed conceptual metaphors in digital newspapers sports articles that are used to conceptualize sports and sportswomen during the 2024 Olympic Games. The corpus consists of 1,411 news written in Spanish extracted from four newspapers: Récord and ESTO from Mexico, and Marca and Mundo Deportivo from Spain. We first identify the conceptual metaphors used in the news and then classify them into metaphorical fields. The discourse-linguistic analysis based on the qualitative data shows that sports and sportswomen are conceptualized through various source domains. With regard to sports, they are mostly conceptualized in terms of SPORTS ARE WAR and SPORTS ARE STORYTELLING in both the Spanish and Mexican corpus. Regarding the representation of women athletes, in both contexts SPORTSWOMEN ARE CHAMPIONS and LEGENDS; however, in Mexico the conceptual metaphor SPORTSWOMEN ARE CHAMPIONS predominates, whereas in Spain SPORTSWOMEN ARE WARRIORS, QUEENS, STARS, MACHINES, or ANIMALS.

title: [Survey on the establishment of smoking areas in city halls in National Association of Directors of Health Departments of Designated Cities, West Block Conference].
title_original: [Survey on the establishment of smoking areas in city halls in National Association of Directors of Health Departments of Designated Cities, West Block Conference].
summary: Objectives In Tokyo, preventing passive smoking progressed during the 32nd Olympic Games. However, smoking areas remain in many local city halls, and tobacco product companies donate smoking areas in front of stations and near parks. A questionnaire survey was conducted at the Western Block Conference of the National Association of Directors of Health Departments of Designated Cities to accurately assess the status of smoking areas established and managed by designated cities.Methods Questionnaires were distributed to the relevant departments in 30 designated cities. Smoking rates in the prefectures in which each designated city is located and tobacco tax revenues by city were collected from comprehensive information provided by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. The Mann-Whitney U test compared smoking rates. Fisher's exact test examined for correlations, with P<0.05 considered significant. Because this study was an analysis of a questionnaire survey conducted among government agencies and open data, an ethics review was deemed unnecessary.Results Fifteen designated cities (50%) had smoking areas in their city halls. The reasons provided were "staff preference" in five cities and "citizen preference" in three. Twenty-four designated cities (80%) had smoking areas donated by tobacco companies. The WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) guidelines were recognized in 18 designated cities (60%). There was no significant difference in smoking prevalence between designated cities with and without smoking areas in their city halls (P = 0.933). FCTC awareness was not significantly related to the presence of smoking areas donated by tobacco companies (P = 1). The presence of smoking areas in city halls and presence of smoking areas donated by tobacco companies had no significant relation (P = 0.651). Drawing a line of 2 billion yen in tobacco tax revenue, designated cities exceeding this threshold were significantly may have smoking areas in their city halls (P = 0.025).Conclusion Smoking areas remain in city halls of designated cities in Western Japan. Although the presence or absence of smoking areas in city halls and smoking rate or donation of smoking areas had no significant relationship, there was a significant relationship with the tobacco tax. Local governments should not install smoking areas to prevent passive smoking.

title: From temporary event spaces to permanent urban communities: A physical-relational-legacy framework for Olympic Village transformation
title_original: From temporary event spaces to permanent urban communities: A physical-relational-legacy framework for Olympic Village transformation
summary: The Olympic Village has evolved over time to become a full-fledged urban system that encompasses not just the temporary housing needs of athletes participating in the Olympic Games but also infrastructure development, governance coordination, sustainability planning, and long-term community transformation. Although there are many studies of Olympic Villages, they typically focus on a single aspect of them such as the physical redevelopment of an area, the way that it was governed during the Olympics, and what happened to the Village after the Games ended. Existing studies have examined various dimensions separately, but fewer studies integrate these dimensions into a unified lifecycle framework. To fill this gap, this study proposed the Physical-Relational-Legacy (P-R-L) framework to help explain the changes in form that occur in Olympic Villages over their lifecycle. Using a Straussian grounded theory approach and comparative case study methodology, the study investigated six Olympic events: the Summer Olympics of 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024, and the Winter Olympics of 2022. The data collected for this study included official Olympic reports, operational manuals, planning documents, and other types of published materials related to legacy. Using systematic open, axial, and selective coding supported by constant comparison, the study inductively developed the three interrelated dimensions: Physical, Relational, and Legacy. The results of this study indicated that the transformation of an Olympic Village is not simply a matter of developing some areas after the games end. Rather, it involves a series of interactions between changing infrastructure systems, governance mechanisms, and ongoing legacy development processes. Moreover, each of these dimensions interacts with one another at all stages of an Olympic Village's lifecycle instead of occurring sequentially. The study contributes by providing an integrated analytical framework explaining how physical adaptation, governance coordination, and legacy formation interact throughout the Olympic Village lifecycle.

title: Athlete-Level Dynamics in Elite Swimming Across Nine Global Championships (2016–2025): Age Structure, Podium Tenure, and Competitive Turnover
title_original: Athlete-Level Dynamics in Elite Swimming Across Nine Global Championships (2016–2025): Age Structure, Podium Tenure, and Competitive Turnover
summary: The elite swimming calendar became substantially denser after 2020. We examined how the individual-event medalist population at the nine global championships of 2016–2025 changed in age structure, podium tenure, medal accumulation, and turnover. All 865 individual-event medals (277 athletes) at three Olympic Games and six World Championships were organized as an athlete-by-edition panel and analyzed with athlete-clustered and wild cluster bootstrap inference, exploratory Bayesian partial pooling, discrete-time hazard models, negative binomial regression, and bootstrap measures of concentration. Mean medalist age ranged from 22.86 to 24.46 years across editions. None of the 34 sex-by-event era contrasts survived false-discovery-rate adjustment; the two with the smallest p-values (men’s 200 m breaststroke, +2.79 years; women’s 400 m individual medley, −5.19 years; both q = 0.062) are exploratory, and both were accompanied by near-complete turnover of the event’s medalists. Median podium tenure was two editions. Each additional year of age at the first observed medal was associated with a higher hazard of a last observed medal (HR 1.106, 95% CI 1.063–1.151) and lower subsequent accumulation (IRR 0.863, 95% CI 0.823–0.904), whereas winning two or more medals at the first observed championship was associated with about half the hazard (HR 0.564, 95% CI 0.364–0.874) and twice the accumulation rate (IRR 2.066, 95% CI 1.410–3.027). The title-defense rate was 58.8% across 2017 → 2019 and 15.4% across the later World Championship transitions (OR 0.128, 95% CI 0.040–0.409), while the Gini coefficient of medal counts ranged from 0.205 to 0.248. Medal concentration remained descriptively similar, while the identities of the winners changed more frequently.

title: A Phenomenological Approach to Understanding Photography:  Essence, Boundaries, and Prospects
title_original: A Phenomenological Approach to Understanding Photography:  Essence, Boundaries, and Prospects
summary: The article elucidates the specificity of the phenomenological approach to the analysis of photography as a cultural and philosophical phenomenon. Drawing on key concepts (E.O. Krank, R. Barthes, J. Derrida, E. Fischer, L.S. Purcell, et al.), the study demonstrates how phenomenology shifts the focus from the attributive properties of the photograph to the perceptual and existential experience of the viewer, thereby revealing the ontological and epistemological significance of the photographic image. Particular attention is paid to the cri-tique of the eidetic model of phenomenology and to the prospects for its development within existential and hermeneutic phenomenology. The article also analyses manifestations of the phenomenological optics in the representation of the tragic and in the functioning of photography in the digital environment. In conclusion, it substantiates the need for a comprehensive approach that takes into account the material, technological, and sociocultural dimensions of the photography functioning.

title: Smart culture: cognitive, ethical, and existential limits of technological evolution
title_original: Smart culture: cognitive, ethical, and existential limits of technological evolution
summary: This study examines transformations in personal value orientations and cognitive mechanisms against the backdrop of ubiquitous smartization. The phenomenon of "smart culture," conceptualized as a complex multilevel system, serves as the object of analysis. This system integrates techno-social practices, algorithmic patterns of behavior, and identity shifts under the influence of smart technologies that have evolved from simple intermediaries into active creators of perception mechanisms. The following key aspects of the problem are delineated: the covert substitution of critical reflection with routine data processing; the reduction of moral choice to simplified binary algorithms; and the ontological lability of the self within the context of continuous network connectivity. Fundamental attention is paid to the immanent contradiction between the declared anthropocentricity of the smart environment and the empirically recorded practice of exploiting users' cognitive potential, whose activity is transformed into transparent raw material for collecting predictive behavioral indicators. The theoretical-methodological foundation – an interdisciplinary synthesis of philosophical anthropology, cognitive neuroscience, and the sociology of technology, augmented by theories of distributed cognition, surveillance economics, and post-structuralist dismantling of identity – is supplemented by empirical data derived from a mass questionnaire survey of 6,057 respondents (schoolchilds and educators of the Ryazan Oblast), conducted by the author in 2025-2026. The scientific novelty of the research lies in formulating the concept of the "immanent exhaustion" of smart culture. This phenomenon is regarded not as a byproduct of external technological or sociocultural threats, but as a dialectical mechanism of self-destruction immanent to the very essence of total quantification and unrestricted algorithmic optimization. The author introduces elements of their proprietary theory into scholarly discourse: "cognitive parasitism" — the suppression of neurocognitive resource formation by algorithms; "ontological dispersion" – the rift between the user's perception of smart technologies and their objective algorithmic nature; alongside a detailed conceptualization of "algorithmic heteronomy" – human moral dependence on machine-mediated decisions masquerading as one's own choice. In conclusion, it is argued that the antagonisms inherent in the contemporary smart environment precondition society's transition to the Seventh Information Revolution and Industry 5.0. According to the author's concept, through the synergistic effect of smartization processes, bioengineering augmentation, and cyborgization, this stage forms the epistemological and ontological foundations for the onset of the Second Quantum Revolution and the emergence of quantum culture, which opens the era of Industry 6.0 for humanity.

title: Ethical frameworks in the context of Agile transformation in IT (the case of Rostelecom)
title_original: Ethical frameworks in the context of Agile transformation in IT (the case of Rostelecom)
summary: The article provides a socio-philosophical reflection on the phenomenon of ethical frameworks that emerge in the process of Agile-transformation of Russian IT companies. The author postulates that these frameworks function not as normative systems, but as discursive practices that produce new forms of sociality and power in the context of "managed self-organization." Synthesizing the methodological apparatus of postmodern philosophy (M. Foucault, J.-F. Lyotard, J. Deleuze and F. Guattari) with sociocultural analysis reveals the process of hybridization as a key mechanism for adapting global management narratives to local conditions. Empirical evidence, based on the case of Rostelecom, demonstrates how these rhizomatic ethical systems legitimize performative effectiveness. The analysis shows how disciplinary control is translated into mechanisms of digital transparency and self-optimization, ultimately forging a new type of corporate subjectivity aligned with the demands of a flexible, post-industrial economy. This study specifically examines the implementation of the "KARMA Framework" at Rostelecom, revealing a hybrid model where the rhetoric of autonomy and self-organization is strategically deployed. The findings illustrate that this adaptation often reinforces existing power structures by digitizing traditional oversight, thereby creating a potent, legitimizing discourse for a modernized form of hierarchical control. The paper introduces and develops the concept of "managed self-organization" as a critical lens to understand this paradoxical power dynamic. It argues that this model represents a form of digital governmentality, where control is exercised not through direct coercion, but through the very architectures of participation and visibility. The research concludes that the resulting ethical framework serves primarily as a technology for shaping a compliant, self-managing subject, highlighting the risks of such hybridization devolving into a full-blown simulacrum of agility, devoid of its emancipatory potential.

title: Features of the conceptualization of the term "mass culture" in western and chinese academic traditions
title_original: Features of the conceptualization of the term "mass culture" in western and chinese academic traditions
summary: The subject of the research is the content and semantic specificity of the concept of "mass culture" in Western (Western European and American) and Chinese academic traditions. The author examines in detail aspects such as interpretations of key terms like "mass," "mass culture," "popular culture," and their synonymous series in English and Chinese. Special attention is given to the historical and cultural context of the formation of these concepts: in the Western tradition, critical approaches by Ortega y Gasset, Macdonald, Horkheimer, and Adorno link mass culture with the culture industry and endow it with negative connotations, and analytical approaches by Birmingham’s turn; in China, the influence of the May Fourth Movement and the activities of the League of Leftist Writers, which shaped the enlightening and ideologically oriented perception of "&#22823;&#20247;&#25991;&#21270;" (mass culture). Within the subject, classifications of types of culture, characteristics of synonymy and antonymy of terms, and the specifics of mass culture functions in each of the examined contexts are analyzed. A comparative analysis is applied to the definition of key concepts in the two cultural traditions. Methods of semantic and terminological analysis, comparison of synonymous and antonymous series in English and Chinese, and a historical-contextual approach are used to identify factors that influenced the formation of interpretations. The methodology relies on critical texts of Western theorists and materials from the Chinese humanities tradition. The novelty of the research lies in the systematic comparison of the semantics and value connotations of the concept of "mass culture" in Western and Chinese academic traditions, based on linguistic and historical-cultural analysis. A significant contribution to the study of the topic is the identification of fundamental differences in the perception of the category "mass" and the functions of mass culture: in Western thought, it is interpreted as a product of the culture industry, associated with manipulation, standardization, and opposition to high culture, then it is considered as a complex field of meaning generation; while in the Chinese context, it is understood as a tool for enlightening the broad masses and an element of ideological integration. The main conclusions are: the existence of two fundamentally different paradigms for understanding mass culture, determined by the specifics of historical and sociocultural development; the significance of its enlightening function in the Chinese tradition as a key meaning-forming factor; and the necessity to consider the cultural-historical context when making intercultural comparisons of terms, as differences in semantics and evaluative connotations reflect fundamental divergences in understanding the role of the "mass" in society.

title: Наследие греческого олимпизма
title_original: Наследие греческого олимпизма
summary: О духовных особенностях и проведении Олимпийских игр Древней Греции (Эллады), вкладе эллинской цивилизации в мировую культуру, нравственность, спорт. Освещено наследование современными олимпийцами присущих эллинам ценностей мирной жизни, гармоничного развития, стремления к личным достижениям. Проанализированы существенные черты первого столетия современного олимпийского движения. Может быть использовано для самообразования, а также в разделах истории, педагогики, философии, эстетики, других учебных дисциплин.
